sentences.zh: 石虎

translations.literal: Shi Hu
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu (taboo name of Shi Jilong)

sentences.zh: ，季龍親耕藉田于其桑梓苑，其妻杜氏祠先蠶於近郊，遂如襄國謁勒墓。

translations.literal: , Jilong personally plowed the sacred field at his Mulberry-and-Catalpa Park; his wife Lady Du sacrificed to the First Silkworm in the outer suburbs; then he proceeded to Xiangguo to visit Shi Le's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At Mulberry-Catalpa Park Jilong handled the spring plowing rite; Lady Du offered to the silkworm goddess near the capital; then they traveled to Xiangguo to sweep Shi Le's tomb.

sentences.zh: 以中書監石寧為征西將軍，率并、司州兵二餘人為麻秋等後繼。

translations.literal: He appointed Palace Secretariat Supervisor Shi Ning General Who Conquers the West, leading more than twenty thousand troops from Bing and Si prefectures as rear support for Ma Qiu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ning marched west with over twenty thousand Bing and Si soldiers to back Ma Qiu's Liangzhou thrust.

sentences.zh: 張重華將宋秦等率戶二萬來降。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua's general Song Qin and others led twenty thousand households to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qin brought Zhang Chonghua twenty thousand households over to Zhao.

sentences.zh: 河湟間氐羌十餘萬落與張璩相首尾，麻秋憚之，不進。

translations.literal: Between He and Huang rivers more than one hundred thousand Di and Qiang settlements coordinated with Zhang Quan; Ma Qiu feared them and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Huangshui frontier hundreds of thousands of Di and Qiang tents coordinated with Zhang Quan; Ma Qiu dared not push.

sentences.zh: 重華金城太守張沖又以郡降石寧。

translations.literal: Chonghua's Administrator of Jincheng Zhang Chong again surrendered the commandery to Shi Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong, governor of Jincheng, opened his gates to Shi Ning.

sentences.zh: 麻秋尋次曲柳，劉甯、王擢進攻晉興武街。

translations.literal: Ma Qiu soon halted at Quwillow; Liu Ning and Wang Zhuo advanced to attack Jinxing's Wujie.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu camped at Quliu while Liu Ning and Wang Zhuo struck toward Jinxing and Wujie.

sentences.zh: 重華將楊康等與甯戰于沙阜，寧敗績，乃引還金城。

translations.literal: Chonghua's general Yang Kang and others fought Ning at Sandy Mound; Ning suffered rout and withdrew to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kang routed Shi Ning at Shaqiu; Ning fled to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 王擢克武街，執重華護軍曹權、胡宣，徙七千餘戶於雍州。

translations.literal: Wang Zhuo took Wujie, capturing Chonghua's Defender Cao Quan and Hu Xuan, relocating more than seven thousand households to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo seized Wujie, bagged Cao Quan and Hu Xuan, and shipped seven thousand families to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 季龍又以孫伏都為征西將軍，與麻秋率步騎三萬長驅濟河，且城長最。

translations.literal: Jilong further appointed Sun Fodu General Who Conquers the West; he and Ma Qiu led thirty thousand infantry and horse on a long drive across the Yellow River and walled Changzui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fodu joined Ma Qiu with thirty thousand men, crossed the Yellow River, and fortified Changzui.

sentences.zh: 重華大懼，遣將謝艾逆擊，敗之，秋退歸金城。

translations.literal: Chonghua was terrified and sent general Xie Ai to strike him in reverse; defeating him, Qiu withdrew to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua panicked; Xie Ai counterattacked and drove Ma Qiu back to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 勒及季龍並貪而無禮，既王有十州之地，金帛珠玉及外國珍奇異貨不可勝紀，而猶以為不足，曩代帝王及先賢陵墓靡不發掘，而取其寶貨焉。

translations.literal: Both Shi Le and Jilong were greedy and without ritual propriety; once they kingly held ten prefectures' territory, gold, silk, pearls, jade, and foreign treasures beyond reckoning, still they deemed it insufficient—former-age emperors and worthies' tombs none they failed to open, taking their treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Father and nephew looted tombs across ten provinces—no grave was sacred once treasure tempted them.

sentences.zh: 邯鄲城西石子堈上有趙簡子墓，至是季龍令發之，初得炭深丈餘，次得木板厚一尺，積板厚八尺，乃及泉，其水清冷非常，作絞車以牛皮囊汲之，月餘而水不盡，不可發而止。

translations.literal: West of Handan city on Stone Mound lay the tomb of Zhao Jianzi; by now Jilong ordered it opened—first came charcoal more than one zhang deep, next planks one chi thick stacked eight chi deep, then reaching spring water whose clarity was extraordinary; they rigged winches with ox-hide bags to bail—a month passed yet water did not end; unable to complete the opening they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They sank shafts through charcoal and oak seals toward Zhao Jianzi's vault until an underground river thwarted the robbers.

sentences.zh: 又使掘秦始皇塚，取銅柱鑄以為器。

translations.literal: He also ordered Qin Shihuang's mound dug and bronze pillars taken to cast vessels.
translations.idiomatic: They melted First Emperor's bronze pillars into pots.

sentences.zh: 時沙門吳進言于季龍曰：「胡運將衰，晉當復興，宜若役晉人以厭其氣。

translations.literal: At that time monk Wu Jin said to Jilong: "Hu fortune will decline and Jin should revive—you ought to exhaust Jin people to suppress their qi.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Wu Jin urged labor gangs of ethnic Jin to break Han resurgence.

sentences.zh: 」季龍於是使尚書張群發近郡男女十六萬，車十萬乘，運土築華林苑及長牆於鄴北，廣長數十里。

translations.literal: " Jilong thereupon ordered Masters of Writing Zhang Qun to levy sixteen thousand men and women from neighboring commanderies and one hundred thousand carts to haul earth building Splendid Grove Park and the long wall north of Ye—several tens of li in breadth and length.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen thousand souls and a hundred thousand carts raised Ye's Pleasure Grove and its miles-long curtain wall.

sentences.zh: 趙攬、申鐘、石璞等上疏陳天文錯亂，蒼生凋弊，及因引見，又面諫，辭旨甚切。

translations.literal: Zhao Lan, Shen Zhong, Shi Pu, and others submitted memorials stating celestial patterns were disordered and common folk withered; when summoned for audience they remonstrated face-to-face with extreme earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers cited skewed stars and starving homes; at audience they spoke bluntly.

sentences.zh: 季龍大怒曰：「牆朝戌夕沒，吾無恨矣。

translations.literal: Jilong raged greatly saying: "If the wall stands morning but sinks evening We have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: "Finish it tonight if it falls tomorrow—I won't mourn.

sentences.zh: 」乃促張群以燭夜作。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he hurried Zhang Qun to labor by candlelight through nights.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qun drove crews under torchlight.

sentences.zh: 起三觀、四門，三門通漳水，皆為鐵扉。

translations.literal: He raised three observatories and four gates; three gates opened to Zhang waters—all iron doors.
translations.idiomatic: Triple towers, quad gates, three iron portals opening on the Zhang.

sentences.zh: 暴風大雨，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Violent wind and great rain—several tens of thousands died.
translations.idiomatic: A freak storm killed tens of thousands on the works.

sentences.zh: 揚州送黃鵠雛五，頸長一丈，聲聞十餘里，泛之于玄武池。

translations.literal: Yangzhou presented five yellow-crane chicks with necks one zhang long whose cries carried over ten li; they floated them on Mystic Warrior Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Five crane chicks from Yangzhou—ten-foot necks, mile-carrying calls—bobbed on the imperial lake.

sentences.zh: 郡國前後送蒼麟十六，白鹿七，季龍命司虞張曷柱調之，以駕芝蓋，列於充庭之乘。

translations.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms successively presented sixteen blue unicorns and seven white deer; Jilong ordered Chief of Waters Zhang Hezhu to train them to pull fungus-pattern canopies in the courtyard carriage ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen teal unicorns and seven white deer pulled fungus-canopied state coaches.

sentences.zh: 鑿北城，引水于華林園。

translations.literal: They cut the north wall channeling water into Splendid Grove Garden.
translations.idiomatic: They breached Ye's north wall to flood the grove.

sentences.zh: 城崩，壓死者百餘人。

translations.literal: The wall collapsed crushing more than a hundred dead.
translations.idiomatic: The breach buried a hundred workers.

sentences.zh: 命石宣祈於山川，因而遊獵，乘大輅，羽葆、華蓋，建天子旌旗，十有六軍，戎卒十八萬，出自金明門。

translations.literal: He ordered Shi Xuan to pray at mountains and rivers, then roam hunting—riding the great chariot with feather canopy and splendor awning, erecting Son-of-Heaven banners—sixteen armies, one hundred eighty thousand armored troops exiting Golden Bright Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan rode the imperial equipage with sixteen hosts—one hundred eighty thousand men—out Golden Bright Gate on a ritual hunt.

sentences.zh: 季龍從其後宮升陵霄觀望之，笑曰：「我家父子如是，自非天崩地陷，當復何愁，但抱子弄孫日為樂耳！

translations.literal: Jilong ascended Lingxiao Watch from his rear palace to gaze, laughing: "Our house father and sons thus—unless heaven collapses and earth sinks, what worry remains—only cradling sons and teasing grandsons for daily pleasure!
translations.idiomatic: From Lingxiao Tower Jilong sneered that only skyfall could touch his clan—otherwise life was toys and toddlers.

sentences.zh: 」宣既馳逐無厭，所在陳列行宮，四面各以百里為度，驅圍禽獸，皆幕集其所。

translations.literal: " Once Xuan galloped without satiation, wherever he went he arrayed traveling palaces—each face taking a hundred li as measure—driving and enclosing beasts and birds until all gathered beneath curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan ringed hundred-li paddocks with silk pavilions and drove game inward.

sentences.zh: 文武跪立，圍守重行，烽炬星羅，光燭如晝，命勁騎百餘馳射其中。

translations.literal: Civil and military knelt in ranks guarding layered lines; beacon fires dotted like stars; light blazed as day; he ordered more than a hundred picked riders to gallop and shoot within.
translations.idiomatic: Officials knelt guard while torches turned night to noon and mounted archers slaughtered penned beasts.

sentences.zh: 宣與嬖姬顯德美人乘輦觀之，嬉娛忘反，獸殫乃止。

translations.literal: Xuan rode a palanquin with favorite Lady Xiande to watch, amusing himself forgetting return until beasts were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He lounged with Lady Xiande in a litter until the kill pens emptied.

sentences.zh: 其有禽獸奔逸，當之者坐，有爵者奪馬步驅一日，無爵者鞭之一百。

translations.literal: If any beast broke bounds, whoever blocked it sat liable—those with rank lost horses and marched one day on foot; those without rank received one hundred lashes.
translations.idiomatic: Escapees cost guards their mounts or skin.

sentences.zh: 峻制嚴刑，文武戰慄，士卒饑凍而死者萬有餘人。

translations.literal: Harsh regulations and cruel punishments made civil and military tremble; soldiers starved and froze to death—more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Draconian rules froze the camp—ten thousand troop deaths.

sentences.zh: 宣弓馬衣食皆號為禦，有亂其間者，以冒禁罪罪之。

translations.literal: Xuan's bows, horses, clothing, and food were all marked imperial—forbidden mixing on pain of violating prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Anything touching the heir's kit meant death.

sentences.zh: 所過三州十五郡，資儲靡有孑遺。

translations.literal: Passing three prefectures and fifteen commanderies, stores left not a survivor.
translations.idiomatic: Three provinces fifteen counties—granaries stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 季龍復命石韜亦如之，出自并州，游于秦、晉。

translations.literal: Jilong again ordered Shi Tao to do likewise, departing Bingzhou to roam Qin and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao mirrored the circus from Bing through Qin and Jin.

sentences.zh: 宣素惡韜寵，是行也，嫉之彌甚。

translations.literal: Xuan had long hated Tao's favor; this journey inflamed envy.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan loathed Shi Tao's favor—envy blazed on tour.

sentences.zh: 宦者趙生得幸于宣而無寵於韜，微勸宣除之，於是相圖之計起矣。

translations.literal: Eunuch Zhao Sheng enjoyed Xuan's favor without Tao's—subtly urging Xuan to eliminate him—thereupon mutual plotting arose.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Sheng whispered murder; princes began stalking each other.

sentences.zh: 麻秋又襲張重華將張瑁於河、陝，敗之，斬首三千餘級。

translations.literal: Ma Qiu again raided Zhang Chonghua's general Zhang Mao at He and Shan, defeating him and taking more than three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu smashed Zhang Mao on the He-Shan line—three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 枹罕護軍李逵率眾七千降于季龍。

translations.literal: Baohan Defender Li Kui led seven thousand followers to surrender to Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui brought seven thousand out of Baohan.

sentences.zh: 自河已南，氐、羌皆降。

translations.literal: South of the Yellow River Di and Qiang all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: South of the river Di and Qiang bent knee.

sentences.zh: 石韜起堂于太尉府，號曰宣光殿，梁長九丈。

translations.literal: Shi Tao raised a hall at Grand Commandant headquarters titled Manifest Light Hall—beams nine zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao's "Manifest Light" reception hall spanned nine-zhang beams.

sentences.zh: 宣視而大怒，斬匠，截梁而去。

translations.literal: Xuan viewed it and raged greatly, executing craftsmen and cutting the beams away.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan beheaded builders and sawed the rafters.

sentences.zh: 韜怒，增之十丈。

translations.literal: Tao raged and extended them to ten zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao rebuilt ten zhang high.

sentences.zh: 宣聞之，恚甚，謂所幸楊柸、牟成曰：「韜凶豎勃逆，敢違我如是！

translations.literal: Hearing this Xuan was furious beyond measure, telling his favorites Yang Bei and Mou Cheng: "That vicious stripling Tao rebels daring to defy me thus!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan told Yang Bei and Mou Cheng Shi Tao had insulted heaven.

sentences.zh: 汝能殺之者，吾入西宮，當盡以韜之國邑分封汝等。

translations.literal: If you can kill him, when I enter the Western Palace I shall entirely divide Tao's state revenues to enfeoff you.
translations.idiomatic: Kill him and his fiefs are yours.

sentences.zh: 韜既死，主上必親臨喪，因行大事，蔑不濟矣。

translations.literal: Once Tao dies the sovereign will surely personally attend mourning—then enact the great deed—nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral draws the emperor—strike then.

sentences.zh: 」柸等許諾。

translations.literal: " Bei and others promised.
translations.idiomatic: They swore.

sentences.zh: 時東南有黃黑雲，大如數畝，稍分為三，狀若匹布，東西經天，色黑而青，酉時貫日，日沒後分為七道，每相去數十丈，間有白雲如魚鱗，子時乃滅。

translations.literal: At that time southeastward appeared yellow-black cloud large like several mu—gradually splitting into three, shaped like bolt silk, east-west spanning heaven—black with green tint—at you hour piercing the sun; after sunset divided into seven tracks each several tens of zhang apart—among them white cloud like fish scales—vanished at zi hour.
translations.idiomatic: Weird vapor split the sky from noon past dusk—omens Shi Tao read as assassination.

sentences.zh: 韜素解天文，見而惡之，顧謂左右曰：「此變不小，當有刺客起于京師，不知誰定當之？

translations.literal: Tao understood astronomy; seeing it he loathed it, looking left and right saying: "This mutation is no small matter—there should arise assassins from the capital—who will surely bear it?
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tao studied stars and guessed a killer stalked the capital.

sentences.zh: 」是夜，韜宴其僚屬于東明觀，樂奏，酒酣，愀然長歎曰：「人居世無常，別易會難。

translations.literal: " That night Tao feasted subordinates at east Mystic Bright Watch—music played, wine deep—he grimaced and sighed long: "Human dwelling in the world lacks constancy—parting easy, meeting hard.
translations.idiomatic: That night at East Mystic Bright terrace he toasted his officers through tears.

sentences.zh: 各付一杯，開意為吾飲，令必醉。

translations.literal: Each take one cup—open hearts and drink for me—command must end drunk.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed every officer to drain a cup.

sentences.zh: 知後會復何期而不飲乎！

translations.literal: Knowing later meetings have unknown dates—how can we not drink!
translations.idiomatic: Future reunions uncertain—wine now.

sentences.zh: 」因泫然流涕，左右莫不歔欷，因宿於佛精舍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon tears streamed; left and right none failed to sniffle—therefore he lodged night at Buddha cloister.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping among friends, he slept in the monastery.

sentences.zh: 宣使楊柸、牟皮、牟成、趙生等緣獼猴梯而入，殺韜，置其刀箭而去。

translations.literal: Xuan sent Yang Bei, Mou Pi, Mou Cheng, Zhao Sheng and others climb monkey ladders to enter, killing Tao, placing his blades and arrows before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Assassins scaled monkey ladders, murdered Shi Tao, and planted daggers.

sentences.zh: 旦，宣奏之。

translations.literal: At dawn Xuan memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Shi Xuan filed his sham report.

sentences.zh: 季龍哀驚氣絕，久之方蘇。

translations.literal: Jilong mourned and started breathless—long before reviving.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong fainted from grief.

sentences.zh: 將出臨之，其司空李農諫曰：「害秦公者恐在蕭牆之內，慮生非常，不可以出。

translations.literal: About to go attend in person, his Minister of Works Li Nong remonstrated: "Those who harmed Prince Qin likely lie within the inner screen—fearing extraordinary birth—you may not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nong warned killers lurked inside the purple curtain.

sentences.zh: 」季龍乃止。

translations.literal: " Jilong thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong stayed put.

sentences.zh: 嚴兵發哀于太武殿。

translations.literal: He ordered strict troops and raised mourning at Grand Martial Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Armored guards staged mourning in Grand Martial Hall.

sentences.zh: 宣乘素車，從千人，臨韜喪，不哭，直言呵呵，使舉衾看屍，大笑而去。

translations.literal: Xuan rode an unadorned cart with a thousand followers attending Tao's funeral—did not weep—only chuckled ha-ha—ordered the shroud lifted to view the corpse—laughed greatly and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan giggled through the wake and peeked under the sheet.

sentences.zh: 收大將軍記室參軍鄭靖、尹武等，將委之以罪。

translations.literal: He seized Grand General's recorder-advisers Zheng Jing, Yin Wu, and others intending to pin guilt on them.
translations.idiomatic: He jailed Shi Tao's secretaries as scapegoats.

sentences.zh: 季龍疑宣之害韜也，謀召之，懼其不入，乃偽言其母哀過危惙。

translations.literal: Jilong suspected Xuan had harmed Tao and plotted to summon him—feared he would not enter—therefore falsely said his mother's grief exceeded danger of collapse.
translations.idiomatic: He used Lady Du's fake collapse as bait.

sentences.zh: 宣不虞己之見疑也，入朝中宮，因而止之。

translations.literal: Xuan did not anticipate himself suspected—entered court at empress palace—thereupon was detained.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan walked into trap at empress palace.

sentences.zh: 建興人史科告稱：「韜死夜，宿東宮長上楊柸家,柸夜與五人從外來，相與語曰：『大事已定，但願大家老壽，吾等何患不富貴』。

translations.literal: A man of Jianxing named Shi Ke reported saying: "The night Tao died he lodged at Eastern Palace senior attendant Yang Bei's home—Bei at night with five men came from outside mutually saying: 'The great deed is settled—only wish the great lord long life—what worry have we of wealth and honor.'
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ke reported Yang Bei's midnight boast.

sentences.zh: 語訖便入。

translations.literal: " Speech finished they entered.
translations.idiomatic: They went indoors.

sentences.zh: 科寢暗中，柸不見也。

translations.literal: Ke slept in darkness—Bei did not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ke hid in shadows.

sentences.zh: 科尋出逃匿。

translations.literal: Ke soon fled hiding.
translations.idiomatic: He fled.

sentences.zh: 俄而柸與二人出求科不得，柸曰：『宿客聞人向語，當殺之斷口舌。

translations.literal: Presently Bei with two men went out seeking Ke without finding—Bei said: 'Lodgers who overheard speech must be killed to cut tongues.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bei hunted witnesses.

sentences.zh: 今而得去，作大事矣。

translations.literal: Now if he escapes we accomplish the great deed.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he escapes the coup holds.

sentences.zh: 』科逾牆獲免。

translations.literal: ' Ke vaulted the wall and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ke cleared the wall.

sentences.zh: 」季龍馳使收之，獲楊柸、牟皮、趙生等。

translations.literal: " Jilong galloped envoys to seize them—capturing Yang Bei, Mou Pi, Zhao Sheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Fast riders seized the plotters.

sentences.zh: 柸、皮尋皆亡去，執趙生而詰之，生具首服。

translations.literal: Bei and Pi soon both fled; arresting Zhao Sheng they interrogated him—Sheng fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bei and Mou Pi escaped; Zhao Sheng confessed.

sentences.zh: 季龍悲怒彌甚，幽宣于席庫，以鐵環穿其頷而鎖之，作數斗木槽，和羹飯，以豬狗法食之。

translations.literal: Jilong's grief and rage doubled; he imprisoned Xuan in mat storehouse—pierced his jaw with iron rings locking him—prepared several-dou wooden trough mixing gruel and rice—fed him by pig-dog method.
translations.idiomatic: They chained Shi Xuan and fed him like livestock.

sentences.zh: 取害韜刀箭舐其血，哀號震動宮殿。

translations.literal: Taking the blades and arrows that harmed Tao he licked their blood—wailing shook palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: They made him taste Shi Tao's blood.

sentences.zh: 積柴鄴北，樹標於其上，標末置鹿盧，穿之以繩，倚梯柴積，送宣於標所，使韜所親宦者郝稚、劉霸拔其發，抽其舌，牽之登梯，上于柴積。

translations.literal: He piled firewood north of Ye, planted a pole atop—pole tip mounted pulley—threaded rope—leaned ladder on pyre—sent Xuan to the pole site—had Tao's intimate eunuchs Hao Zhi and Liu Ba pull his hair, extract his tongue, drag him up ladder onto the stack.
translations.idiomatic: A hoisted stake north of Ye awaited the heir.

sentences.zh: 郝稚雙繩貫其頷，鹿盧絞上，劉霸斷其手足，斫眼潰腹，如韜之傷。

translations.literal: Hao Zhi threaded twin ropes through his jaw—pulley winching upward—Liu Ba severed hands and feet, gouged eyes and burst belly matching Tao's wounds.
translations.idiomatic: They winched and dismembered him as Shi Tao had fallen.

sentences.zh: 四面縱火，煙炎際天。

translations.literal: They ignited on four sides—smoke and flame joined heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Four-corner fire climbed skyward.

sentences.zh: 季龍從昭儀已下數千登中臺以觀之。

translations.literal: Jilong from Worthy Consort downward several thousand ascended Central Terrace to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands from consorts down watched Central Terrace.

sentences.zh: 火滅，取灰分置諸門交道中。

translations.literal: Fire extinguished—they gathered ash dividing among major gate crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: Ash went to every crossroads.

sentences.zh: 殺其妻子九人。

translations.literal: He killed his wife and nine children.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and nine children died.

sentences.zh: 宣小子年數歲，季龍甚愛之，抱之而泣。

translations.literal: Xuan's young son several years old—Jilong greatly loved him—embracing wept.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong hugged a toddler grandson and wept.

sentences.zh: 兒曰：「非兒罪。

translations.literal: The child said: "It is not child's crime.
translations.idiomatic: The boy whispered he was innocent.

sentences.zh: 」季龍欲赦之，其大臣不聽，遂於抱中取而戮之，兒猶挽季龍衣而大叫，時人莫不為之流涕，季龍因此發病。

translations.literal: " Jilong wished to pardon him—great ministers refused—thereupon took him from the embrace and executed him—the child still clutched Jilong's robes shouting greatly—people of the time none failed to weep for him—Jilong thereby fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers forced the child's execution—ripping him from Jilong's sleeve broke the emperor.

sentences.zh: 又誅其四率已下三百人，宦者五十人，皆車裂節解，棄之漳水。

translations.literal: He further executed more than three hundred below the Four Escorts rank—fifty eunuchs—all torn by carts and joint-dissected—discarded in Zhang waters.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred guards and fifty eunuchs torn apart—corpses in the Zhang.

sentences.zh: 洿其東宮，養豬牛。

translations.literal: He flooded the Eastern Palace raising pigs and cattle.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's palace became barnyard.

sentences.zh: 東宮衛士十餘萬人皆謫戍涼州。

translations.literal: More than one hundred thousand Eastern Palace guardsmen were all banished to garrison Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand guards banished west.

sentences.zh: 先是，散騎常侍趙攬言于季龍曰：「中宮將有變，宜防之。

translations.literal: Earlier Regular Palace Attendant Zhao Lan had said to Jilong: "The inner palace will suffer mutation—ought to guard against it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lan had warned of palace coup.

sentences.zh: 」及宣之殺韜也，季龍疑其知而不告，亦誅之。

translations.literal: " When Xuan killed Tao Jilong suspected he knew yet did not report—thereupon executed him too.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong executed Zhao Lan for withholding.

sentences.zh: 廢宣母杜氏為庶人。

translations.literal: He degraded Xuan's mother Lady Du to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Du fell to commoner rank.

sentences.zh: 貴嬪柳氏，尚書耆之女也，以才色特幸，坐其二兄有寵于宣，亦殺之。

translations.literal: Noble Concubine Lady Liu—daughter of Masters of Writing Liu Qi—with talent and beauty enjoyed special favor—because her two elder brothers enjoyed Xuan's favor—she was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu died for her brothers' tie to Shi Xuan.

sentences.zh: 季龍追其姿色，復納耆少女于華林園。

translations.literal: Jilong regretted her beauty and took Liu Qi's younger daughter into Splendid Grove Garden.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced her with her younger sister.

sentences.zh: 季龍議立太子，其太尉張舉進曰：「燕公斌、彭城公遵並有武藝文德。

translations.literal: Jilong deliberated establishing crown prince; Grand Commandant Zhang Ju advanced comment: "Prince Yan Shi Bin and Prince Pengcheng Shi Zun both possess martial skill and civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju nominated Shi Bin and Shi Zun.

sentences.zh: 陛下神齒已衰，四海未一，請擇二公而樹之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's strength already wanes—the four seas not unified—please choose between the two lords and establish one.
translations.idiomatic: With vigor failing and the realm split, pick Shi Bin or Shi Zun.

sentences.zh: 」初，戎昭張豺之破上邽也，獲劉曜幼女，年十二，有殊色，季龍得而嬖之，生子世，封齊公。

translations.literal: " Earlier when Martial Glory Zhang Chao broke Shanggui he captured Liu Yao's infant daughter—twelve sui—with extraordinary beauty—Jilong obtained and doted on her—bore son Shi Shi—enfeoffed Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao's Liangzhou spoils included Liu Yao's twelve-year-old daughter—mother of prince Shi Shi.

sentences.zh: 至是，豺以季龍年長多疾，規立世為嗣，劉當為太后，己得輔政，說季龍曰：「陛下再立儲宮，皆出自倡賤，是以禍亂相尋。

translations.literal: By now Chao, because Jilong grew old with many ailments, schemed to establish Shi Shi as heir—Lady Liu becoming empress dowager—himself attaining regency—urged Jilong saying: "Your Majesty twice established heirs—both born of singing-girl lowliness—therefore disaster and chaos succeeded one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao pushed Shi Shi so Lady Liu could rule—and he govern.

sentences.zh: 今宜擇母貴子孝者立之。

translations.literal: Now ought to choose mother noble son filial to establish.
translations.idiomatic: Elevate a high-born, dutiful son.

sentences.zh: 」季龍曰：「卿且勿言，吾知太子處矣。

translations.literal: " Jilong said: "Speak no further for now—We know where the heir stands.
translations.idiomatic: Jilong hinted his choice.

sentences.zh: 」又議於東堂，季龍曰：「吾欲以純灰三斛洗吾腹，腹穢惡，故生凶子，兒年二十餘便欲殺公。

translations.literal: " Again deliberating at east hall Jilong said: "We wish to take three hu pure ash and wash Our belly—belly filthy evil—therefore bore vicious sons—sons past twenty sui then wished to kill elders.
translations.idiomatic: At east hall he cursed his womb for breeding parricides.

sentences.zh: 今世方十歲，比其二十，吾已老矣。

translations.literal: Now Shi Shi is only ten sui—by the time he reaches twenty We shall already be old.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shi was ten—by twenty Jilong expected senescence.

sentences.zh: 」於是與張舉、李農定議，敕公卿上書請立世。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with Zhang Ju and Li Nong fixed deliberation—ordering dukes and ministers memorialize requesting Shi Shi be established.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed pact with Zhang Ju and Li Nong to crown Shi Shi.

sentences.zh: 大司農曹莫不署名，季龍使張豺問其故。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture Cao Mo did not affix his signature; Jilong sent Zhang Chao to ask him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Minister of Agriculture Cao Mo withheld his signature, Shi Hu—Jilong—dispatched Zhang Chao to demand an explanation.

sentences.zh: 莫頓首曰：「天下業重，不宜立少，是以不敢署也。

translations.literal: Mo knocked his head on the ground and said: "The enterprise of All-under-Heaven is weighty; it is not fitting to establish the young; therefore I dare not sign."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mo kowtowed and answered, "The realm is too heavy a burden to lay on a child—that is why I could not put my name to the deed."

sentences.zh: 」季龍曰：「莫，忠臣也，然未達朕意。

translations.literal: " Jilong said: "Mo is a loyal subject, yet he has not grasped Our intention."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu replied, "Cao Mo is a faithful minister; he simply does not see what I mean."

sentences.zh: 張舉、李農知吾心矣，其令諭之。

translations.literal: Zhang Ju and Li Nong know Our mind; order them to explain it to him."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhang Ju and Li Nong already understand my purpose—have them make it clear to him."

sentences.zh: 」遂立世為皇太子，劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he established Shi as heir apparent and the Liu clan woman as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He then named Shi Shi crown prince and invested Lady Liu as empress.

sentences.zh: 季龍召太常條攸、光祿勳杜嘏謂之曰：「煩卿傅太子，實希改轍，吾之相托，卿宜明之。

translations.literal: Jilong summoned Grand Master of Ceremonies Tiao You and Superintendent of the Household Du Gu and said to them: "We trouble you two to tutor the heir; We truly hope for a change of course; as for Our entrusting this matter to you, you ought to understand it clearly."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu called in Tiao You, grand master of ceremonies, and Du Gu, superintendent of the household, and told them, "I ask you to instruct the heir and truly wish him to mend his ways; what I am handing you, you must take to heart."

sentences.zh: 」署攸太傅，嘏為少傅。

translations.literal: " He appointed You grand tutor and Gu junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He named Tiao You grand tutor and Du Gu junior tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 季龍時疾瘳，以僭即皇帝位於南郊，大赦境內，建元曰太寧。

translations.literal: When at that time Jilong's illness had abated, he usurped the imperial title at the southern suburb, granted a general amnesty within the borders, and established the era name Great Tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Hu had rallied from his sickness, he arrogated the throne at the southern suburban altar, proclaimed an empire-wide amnesty, and adopted the reign title Tauning.

sentences.zh: 百官增位一等，諸子進爵郡王。

translations.literal: All officials had their positions raised one grade; his various sons were advanced in noble rank to princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister gained a step in rank, and his sons were promoted to princes of commanderies.

sentences.zh: 以尚書張良為右僕射。

translations.literal: He appointed Masters-of-Writing Zhang Liang as right vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang of the secretariat was made right vice-director.

sentences.zh: 故東宮謫卒高力等萬餘人當戍涼州，行達雍城，既不在赦例，又敕雍州刺史張茂送之。

translations.literal: Former eastern-palace degraded soldiers called the Gao Li, more than ten thousand men, were due to be garrisoned in Liangzhou; en route they reached Yongcheng; they were not within the categories of amnesty, and moreover an edict ordered Yongzhou Governor Zhang Mao to escort them on.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten thousand demoted eastern-palace toughs known as the Gao Li were bound for Liangzhou; when they reached Yongcheng they fell outside the amnesty, and the throne ordered Governor Zhang Mao to march them onward.

sentences.zh: 茂皆奪其馬，令步推鹿車，致糧戍所。

translations.literal: Mao seized all their horses, ordered them to go on foot pushing deer carts, and had grain delivered to the garrison place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao confiscated their mounts and made them haul supplies on foot in handcarts all the way to the posting.

sentences.zh: 高力督定陽梁犢等害眾心之怨，謀起兵東還，陰令胡人頡獨鹿微告戍者，戍者皆踴抃大呼。

translations.literal: Gao Li supervisor Liang Du of Dingyang and others nursed the resentment boiling in every breast, plotted to raise troops and return east, secretly ordered the Hu man Xiedulu to hint to the garrison men, and the garrison men all leaped, clapped, and shouted.
translations.idiomatic: Their overseer Liang Du of Dingyang and his comrades, burning with the men's grievances, plotted an eastern mutiny; Xiedulu quietly tipped off the conscripts, who burst into cheers and stamped their approval.

sentences.zh: 梁犢乃自稱晉征東大將軍，率眾攻陷下辯，逼張茂為大都督、大司馬，載以軺車。

translations.literal: Liang Du then styled himself Jin's General Who Conquers the East, led the host to storm and take Xiabian, compelled Zhang Mao to become grand commander-in-chief and grand marshal, and conveyed him in a light carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Du declared himself Jin's eastern-expedition commander, seized Xiabian, forced Zhang Mao to take the titles of grand commander and grand marshal, and paraded him in an open coach.

sentences.zh: 安西劉甯自安定擊之，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Anxi Liu Ning struck them from Anding and was greatly defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning, the western pacifier, attacked from Anding and limped back in rout.

sentences.zh: 秦、雍間城戍無不摧陷，斬二千石長史，長驅而東。

translations.literal: Between Qin and Yong no city garrison failed to be shattered; they beheaded administrators of two-thousand-shi salary rank and drove straight east.
translations.idiomatic: Fort after fort between Qin and Yong fell; they slew salary-rank governors and swept eastward without pause.

sentences.zh: 高力等皆多力善射，一當十餘人，雖無兵甲，所在掠百姓大斧，施一丈柯，攻戰若神，所向崩潰，戍卒皆隨之，比至長安，眾已十萬。

translations.literal: The Gao Li and their like were all strong of arm and skilled at archery; one man matched more than ten; though they lacked armor and weapons, wherever they went they plundered the common people's great axes, fitted shafts of one zhang, fought as if divine, and wherever they aimed lines collapsed; garrison troops all followed them; by the time they reached Chang'an, the host already numbered one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Those Gao Li fighters were archers and brawlers who could each hold off a dozen men; unarmed, they seized farmers' broadaxes, mounted them on ten-foot helves, and swept through defenses like spirits until every garrison joined them—by Chang'an their horde had swollen to a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 其樂平王石苞時鎮長安，盡銳距之，一戰而敗。

translations.literal: Prince of Leping Shi Bao at that time was stationed at Chang'an; he committed his sharpest troops to resisting them and was defeated in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao, prince of Leping, held Chang'an and threw his best troops against the rebels, only to lose at the first clash.

sentences.zh: 犢遂東出潼關，進如洛川。

translations.literal: Liang Du then went east out of Tong Pass and advanced toward the Luochuan region.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Du broke east through Tong Pass and rolled on toward the Luoyang basin.

sentences.zh: 季龍以李農為大都督，行大將軍事，統衛軍張賀度、征西張良、征虜石閔等，率步騎十萬討之。

translations.literal: Jilong appointed Li Nong as grand commander-in-chief, acting grand general's duties, commanding guards-army Zhang Hedu, western campaign Zhang Liang, captive-quelling Shi Min, and others, and led one hundred thousand infantry and horse to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu named Li Nong commander-in-chief with plenipotentiary general's powers, put Zhang Hedu, Zhang Liang, Shi Min, and others under him, and sent a hundred thousand horse and foot to crush the rising.

sentences.zh: 戰于新安，農師不利。

translations.literal: They fought at Xin'an; Li Nong's army fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: Battle joined at Xin'an, and Li Nong's line buckled.

sentences.zh: 又戰于洛陽，農師又敗，乃退壁成皋。

translations.literal: Again they fought at Luoyang; Li Nong's army was again defeated; thereupon he withdrew and fortified at Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: A second clash at Luoyang broke him again, so he pulled back and dug in at Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 犢東掠滎陽、陳留諸郡，季龍大懼，以燕王石斌為大都督中外諸軍事，率精騎一萬，統姚弋仲、苻洪等擊犢于滎陽東，大敗之，斬犢首而還，討其餘黨，盡滅之。

translations.literal: Liang Du raided east through Xingyang, Chenliu, and the various commanderies; Jilong was greatly afraid; he appointed Prince of Yan Shi Bin as grand commander-in-chief of all military affairs within and without, led ten thousand picked cavalry, commanded Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, and others, and struck Liang Du east of Xingyang, greatly defeated him, beheaded Liang Du and returned, punished his remaining faction, and utterly extinguished them.
translations.idiomatic: As Liang Du pillaged Xingyang and Chenliu, Shi Hu panicked; he gave Shi Bin, prince of Yan, supreme command, ten thousand elite riders, and lieutenants Yao Yizhong and Fu Hong, shattered Liang Du east of Xingyang, brought back his head, and extirpated the rest of his party.

sentences.zh: 俄而晉將軍王龕拔其沛郡。

translations.literal: Before long Jin general Wang Kan captured their Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jin's Wang Kan ripped Pei commandery from Zhao hands.

sentences.zh: 始平人馬勖起兵于洛氏葛谷，自稱將軍。

translations.literal: A man of Shiping, Ma Xu, raised troops at Luoshi Ge Valley and styled himself general.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xu of Shiping rose in Luoshi Ge Valley and proclaimed himself a general.

sentences.zh: 石苞攻滅之，誅三千餘家。

translations.literal: Shi Bao attacked and destroyed him, executing more than three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao stamped out the band and put over three thousand households to the sword.

sentences.zh: 時熒惑犯積屍，又犯昴、月，及熒惑北犯河鼓。

translations.literal: At that time Mars encroached on the Pile of Corpses asterism, also encroached on Mao and the moon, and Mars went north to encroach on River Drum.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent Mars across the Pile of Corpses, across the Pleiades and the moon, and north toward the River Drum stars—a grim sky.

sentences.zh: 未幾，季龍疾甚，以石遵為大將軍，鎮關右，石斌為丞相、錄尚書事，張豺為鎮衛大將軍、領軍將軍、吏部尚書，並受遺輔政。

translations.literal: Before long Jilong's illness was severe; he appointed Shi Zun as grand general guarding the land west of the passes, Shi Bin as chancellor and recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, Zhang Chao as grand general who guards the realm, commanding-general of the army, and minister of personnel, all receiving testamentary mandate to assist rule.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu soon sank mortally ill; he named Shi Zun grand general for the Guanzhong west, Shi Bin chancellor with custody of the secretariat, and Zhang Chao capital guardian, army commander, and personnel minister—each charged by deathbed edict to steer the state.

sentences.zh: 劉氏懼斌之輔政也害世，與張豺謀誅之。

translations.literal: Lady Liu feared that if Bin assisted rule he would harm Shi; she plotted with Zhang Chao to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu feared Shi Bin as regent would murder young Shi Shi; she conspired with Zhang Chao to kill him first.

sentences.zh: 斌時在襄國，乃遣使詐斌曰：「主上患已漸損，王須獵者，可小停也。

translations.literal: Bin was at Xiangguo; she then sent an envoy falsely telling Bin: "The sovereign's ailment has gradually lessened; if the king needs hunting, he may pause a little."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bin was in Xiangguo; she sent a messenger with a lie: "The emperor is mending; if you mean to hunt, you may linger awhile."

sentences.zh: 」斌性好酒耽獵，遂遊畋縱飲。

translations.literal: Bin by nature loved wine and was addicted to hunting; thereupon he roamed hunting and drank without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bin loved wine and the chase; he gave himself to hunts and drinking binges.

sentences.zh: 劉氏矯命稱斌無忠孝之心，免斌官，以王歸第，使張豺弟雄率龍騰五百人守之。

translations.literal: Lady Liu forged orders saying Bin lacked loyal and filial heart, dismissed Bin from office, ordered him as a prince to return to his mansion, and sent Zhang Chao's brother Zhang Xiong leading five hundred Dragon Surge troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: She forged an edict accusing Shi Bin of disloyalty, stripped his offices, sent the prince home under house arrest, and posted Zhang Xiong with five hundred Dragon Surge guards.

sentences.zh: 石遵自幽州至鄴，敕朝堂受拜，配禁兵三萬遣之，遵慟泣而去。

translations.literal: Shi Zun came from Youzhou to Ye; he was ordered to receive appointment at the court hall, was allotted thirty thousand palace guards and dispatched; Zun wept bitterly and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun rode from Youzhou to Ye, was made to take his commission in open court, handed thirty thousand household troops, and sent away weeping.

sentences.zh: 是日季龍疾小瘳，問曰：「遵至未？

translations.literal: That day Jilong's illness slightly abated; he asked: "Has Zun arrived?"
translations.idiomatic: That same day Shi Hu briefly rallied and asked, "Has Shi Zun come?"

sentences.zh: 」左右答言久已去矣。

translations.literal: " Those at his side answered that long ago he had already gone.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said he had left long since.

sentences.zh: 季龍曰：「恨不見之。

translations.literal: Jilong said: "We regret not having seen him."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu murmured, "How I wish I could have seen him."

sentences.zh: 」季龍臨於西閣，龍騰將軍、中郎二百餘人列拜於前。

translations.literal: " Jilong attended at the western gallery; more than two hundred Dragon Surge generals and gentlemen-of-the-household lined up and bowed before him.
translations.idiomatic: He received them at the western gallery, where over two hundred Dragon Surge officers and household gentlemen bowed in ranks.

sentences.zh: 季龍曰：「何所求也？

translations.literal: Jilong said: "What do you seek?"
translations.idiomatic: "What do you want of me?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 」皆言聖躬不和，宜令燕王入宿衛，典兵馬，或言乞為皇太子。

translations.literal: " They all said the sacred person was unwell; Yan Wang ought to enter to guard overnight and command troops and horses; some begged to become crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: They pleaded that the sovereign was failing and the prince of Yan should enter to command the guard; others clamored to be named heir.

sentences.zh: 季龍不知斌之廢也，責曰：「燕王不在內邪？

translations.literal: Jilong did not know Bin had been dismissed; he rebuked them, saying: "Is not the Prince of Yan within?"
translations.idiomatic: Unaware Shi Bin had been cashiered, Shi Hu snapped, "Is not the prince of Yan already inside?"

sentences.zh: 呼來！

translations.literal: Call him here!"
translations.idiomatic: "Summon him at once!"

sentences.zh: 」左右言王酒病，不能入。

translations.literal: " Those at his side said the king was ill from wine and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: They answered that the prince was drunk-sick and could not come.

sentences.zh: 季龍曰：「促持輦迎之，當付其璽綬。

translations.literal: Jilong said: "Hurry—take a palanquin to welcome him; We shall hand him the seals and cords."
translations.idiomatic: "Send a litter—quickly," Shi Hu ordered. "I will give him the seals myself."

sentences.zh: 」亦竟無行者。

translations.literal: " Yet in the end none went.
translations.idiomatic: No one moved to obey.

sentences.zh: 尋昏眩而入。

translations.literal: Shortly he entered in dizziness.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later he collapsed into a stupor.

sentences.zh: 張豺使弟雄等矯季龍命殺斌，劉氏又矯命以豺為太保、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，加千兵百騎，一依霍光輔漢故事。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao had his brother Xiong and others forge Jilong's order to kill Bin; Lady Liu again forged orders appointing Zhang Chao grand guardian, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, adding a thousand infantry and hundred horse in guard, entirely according to the precedent of Huo Guang assisting Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao's brother Xiong forged an order executing Shi Bin; Liu forged another elevating Zhang Chao to grand guardian, supreme commander, and secretariat overseer with a thousand foot and a hundred horse—aping Huo Guang's regency over Han.

sentences.zh: 侍中徐統歎曰：「禍將作矣，吾無為豫之。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-chief Xu Tong sighed: "Calamity is about to arise; I will not put myself among those who prepare for it beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Xu Tong groaned, "The storm is coming—I want no part of the schemes ahead."

sentences.zh: 」乃仰藥而死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed poison and died.

sentences.zh: 俄而季龍亦死。

translations.literal: Before long Jilong also died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Hu followed him to the grave.

sentences.zh: 季龍始以僭立，至此，凡在位十五歲。

translations.literal: Jilong had begun by usurping the throne; reaching this point, altogether he had occupied the throne fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: From his seizure of the throne to this hour Shi Hu had reigned fifteen years.

sentences.zh: 石世

translations.literal: Shi Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: the boy emperor Shi Shi.

sentences.zh: 於是世即偽位，尊劉氏為皇太后，臨朝，進張豺為丞相。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shi succeeded to the false throne, honored Lady Liu as empress dowager with court regency, and advanced Zhang Chao to chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shi mounted the puppet throne, raised Lady Liu to ruling empress dowager, and made Zhang Chao chancellor.

sentences.zh: 豺請石遵、石鑒為左右丞相，以尉其心，劉氏從之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao requested Shi Zun and Shi Jian as left and right chancellors to soothe their hearts; Lady Liu followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao named Shi Zun and Shi Jian left and right chancellors to buy their loyalty; Liu agreed.

sentences.zh: 豺與張舉謀誅李農，而舉與農素善，以豺謀告之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao plotted with Zhang Ju to kill Li Nong, but Zhang Ju was on good terms with Li Nong and informed Li Nong of Zhang Chao's plot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao and Zhang Ju planned Li Nong's murder, yet Zhang Ju, Li Nong's friend, leaked the plot.

sentences.zh: 農懼，率騎百餘奔廣宗，率乞活數萬家保于上白。

translations.literal: Li Nong feared, led more than a hundred horsemen and fled to Guangzong, and led several tens of thousands of Qiehuo households to hold Shangbai.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Li Nong galloped to Guangzong with a hundred riders and rallied tens of thousands of Qiehuo refugee families on Mount Shangbai.

sentences.zh: 劉氏使張舉等統宿衛精卒圍之。

translations.literal: Lady Liu sent Zhang Ju and others to command elite palace-guard troops to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu dispatched Zhang Ju with the household elite to invest the mountain.

sentences.zh: 豺以張離為鎮軍大將軍、監中外諸軍事、司隸校尉，為己之副。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao appointed Zhang Li as grand general who stabilizes the army, overseer of all military affairs within and without, metropolitan governor, as his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao made Zhang Li army-stabilizing commander, overseer of all forces, metropolitan governor, and his second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 鄴中群盜大起，迭相劫掠。

translations.literal: In Ye bandits arose in great numbers, repeatedly raiding one another.
translations.idiomatic: Ye erupted in robbery as gangs preyed on one another.

sentences.zh: 石遵聞季龍之死，屯於河內。

translations.literal: When Shi Zun heard of Jilong's death, he encamped at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Shi Hu's death, Shi Zun halted his army at Henei.

sentences.zh: 姚弋仲、苻洪、石閔、劉甯及武衛王鸞、甯西王午、石榮、王鐵、立義將軍段勤等既平秦、洛，班師而歸，遇遵于李城，說遵曰：「殿下長而且賢，先帝亦有意于殿下矣。

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, Shi Min, Liu Ning, and martial guard Wang Luan, western pacification Wang Wu, Shi Rong, Wang Tie, righteous-establishment general Duan Qin and others, having pacified Qin and Luo, rotated the army home, met Zun at Licheng, and urged Zun, saying: "Your Highness is eldest and worthy; the late emperor also had intentions toward Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, Shi Min, Liu Ning, Wang Luan of the martial guard, Wang Wu of western pacification, Shi Rong, Wang Tie, Duan Qin the righteous-establishment general, and the rest—fresh from pacifying Qin and Luoyang—ran into Shi Zun at Licheng and pleaded, "You are the eldest worthy prince; the late emperor already favored you.

sentences.zh: 但以末年惛惑，為張豺所誤。

translations.literal: Only because in his closing years he was muddled and deluded was he misled by Zhang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Only his final confusion let Zhang Chao lead him astray."

sentences.zh: 今上白相持未下，京師宿衛空虛，若聲張豺之罪，鼓行而討之，孰不倒戈開門而迎殿下者邪！

translations.literal: Now Shangbai still stalemates unconquered; the capital's palace guard stands empty; if we proclaim Zhang Chao's crimes and march with drums beating to punish him, who would not turn halberds and open gates to welcome Your Highness!"
translations.idiomatic: Shangbai still holds out and the capital guard is hollow—denounce Zhang Chao and march in formation, and every soldier will drop his weapon and throw open the gates for you!"

sentences.zh: 」遵從之。

translations.literal: Zun followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun took their counsel.

sentences.zh: 洛州刺史劉國等亦率洛陽之眾至於李城。

translations.literal: Luozhou Governor Liu Guo and others also led Luoyang's host and arrived at Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guo, governor of Luozhou, marched the Luoyang garrison to join them at Licheng.

sentences.zh: 遵檄至鄴，張豺大懼，馳召上白之軍。

translations.literal: When Zun's proclamation reached Ye, Zhang Chao was greatly afraid and urgently recalled the army at Shangbai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao panicked when Shi Zun's manifesto hit Ye and frantically pulled the Shangbai siege army home.

sentences.zh: 遵次於蕩陰，戎卒九萬，石閔為前鋒。

translations.literal: Zun halted at Dangyin; field troops numbered ninety thousand; Shi Min was vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun camped at Dangyin with ninety thousand veterans and Shi Min spearheading the column.

sentences.zh: 豺將出距之，耆舊羯士皆曰：「天子兒來奔喪，吾當出迎之，不能為張豺城戍也。

translations.literal: When Zhang Chao was about to go out to resist them, the elderly Jie warriors all said: "The Son of Heaven's son has come to mourn the funeral; we ought to go out to welcome him; we cannot be wall-and-garrison men for Zhang Chao."
translations.idiomatic: As Zhang Chao prepared to meet them in the field, gray-haired Jie soldiers shouted, "The emperor's son rides to bury his father—we should welcome him, not man Zhang Chao's ramparts."

sentences.zh: 」逾城而出，豺斬之不能止。

translations.literal: " They climbed over the walls and went out; Zhang Chao executed them but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: They scaled the walls to desert; Zhang Chao slaughtered them but could not stem the tide.

sentences.zh: 張離率龍騰二千斬關迎遵。

translations.literal: Zhang Li led two thousand Dragon Surge troops to cut through the barrier and welcome Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li smashed a gate with two thousand Dragon Surge troops and ushered Shi Zun inside.

sentences.zh: 劉氏懼，引張豺入，對之悲哭曰：「先帝梓宮未殯，而禍難繁興。

translations.literal: Lady Liu feared, led Zhang Chao in, and wept miserably to him, saying: "The late emperor's catafalque has not yet been buried, yet disasters multiply and arise.
translations.idiomatic: Terror-stricken, Lady Liu drew Zhang Chao in and sobbed, "The late ruler still lies unburied while calamities pile up.

sentences.zh: 今皇嗣沖幼，托之于將軍，將軍何以匡濟邪？

translations.literal: Now the imperial heir is young and tender; We entrust him to you, general—how will you rescue and aid?"
translations.idiomatic: The boy on the throne is helpless—I lean on you, general—how will you save us?"

sentences.zh: 加遵重官，可以弭不？

translations.literal: Add Zun high office—can it quell this?"
translations.idiomatic: Would stacking honors on Shi Zun quiet this storm?"

sentences.zh: 」豺惶怖失守，無復籌計，但言唯唯。

translations.literal: " Zhang Chao was panic-stricken and lost his guard, had no further schemes, and only said yes-yes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao went blank with fright, offered no plan, and muttered empty assent.

sentences.zh: 劉氏令以遵為丞相、領大司馬、大都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，加黃鉞、九錫，增封十郡，委以阿衡之任。

translations.literal: Lady Liu ordered Zun appointed chancellor, concurrently grand marshal, grand commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, adding golden battle-axe and nine bestowals, increasing fief by ten commanderies, entrusting him with the burden of prime minister like Yi Yin.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered Shi Zun made chancellor, grand marshal, supreme commander, secretariat overseer, golden-axe bearer, nine-insignia recipient, and holder of ten added commanderies—the full weight of chief minister.

sentences.zh: 遵至安陽亭，張豺懼而出迎，遵命執之。

translations.literal: When Zun reached Anyang pavilion, Zhang Chao feared and came out to welcome him; Zun ordered him seized.
translations.idiomatic: At Anyang pavilion Zhang Chao crept out to greet Shi Zun, who had him arrested on the spot.

sentences.zh: 於是貫甲曜兵，入自鳳陽門，升于太武前殿，擗踴盡哀，退如東閣。

translations.literal: Thereupon they donned armor and displayed weapons, entered by Fengyang Gate, ascended the Grand Martial front hall, beat their breasts and stamped in full mourning, then withdrew to the eastern gallery.
translations.idiomatic: Armored and banners blazing, they entered through Fengyang Gate, climbed the Grand Martial hall to keen and drum their grief, then retired to the eastern wing.

sentences.zh: 斬張豺于平樂市，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao was beheaded at Pingle market; his three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao died on Pingle market scaffold, his three kinships extirpated.

sentences.zh: 假劉氏令曰：「嗣子幼沖，先帝私恩所授，皇業至重，非所克堪。

translations.literal: Forging Lady Liu's order it said: "The heir is young and tender; he was appointed by the late emperor's private favor; the imperial enterprise is supremely weighty—not what he can bear.
translations.idiomatic: A forged rescript in Liu's voice read, "The boy was enthroned by a father's whim; the mandate is too vast for him.

sentences.zh: 其以遵嗣位。

translations.literal: Let Zun succeed to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Let Shi Zun inherit the throne."

sentences.zh: 」遵偽讓至於再三，群臣敦勸，乃受之，僭即尊位於太武前殿，大赦殊死已下，罷上白圍。

translations.literal: Zun falsely declined reaching thrice; the ministers urgently urged; then he accepted, usurped the supreme title at the Grand Martial front hall, granted general amnesty short of capital crimes, and lifted the siege of Shangbai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun thrice refused the crown until his ministers pressed him; then he seized the throne in the Grand Martial hall, amnested all but capital crimes, and raised the siege of Shangbai.

sentences.zh: 封世為譙王，邑萬戶待以不臣之禮，廢劉氏為太妃，尋皆殺之。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Shi as Prince of Qiao with ten thousand households and treated him with the rites due one who is not a subject; he demoted Lady Liu to senior consort; before long both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He made Shi Shi prince of Qiao with a ten-thousand-household fief yet honored him like a peer, reduced Lady Liu to senior consort, and soon murdered them both.

sentences.zh: 世凡立三十三日。

translations.literal: Shi had altogether occupied the position thirty-three days.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shi had ruled thirty-three days in all.

sentences.zh: 石遵

translations.literal: Shi Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: Shi Zun.

sentences.zh: 於是李農歸請罪，遵復其位，待之如初。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Nong returned to ask forgiveness; Zun restored his position and treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nong came back to plead guilt; Shi Zun restored his offices and favored him as before.

sentences.zh: 尊其母鄭氏為皇太后，其妻張氏為皇后，以石斌子衍為皇太子，石鑒為侍中，石沖為太保，石苞為大司馬，石琨為大將軍，石閔為中外諸軍事、輔國大將軍、錄尚書事，輔政。

translations.literal: He honored his mother Lady Zheng as empress dowager, his wife Lady Zhang as empress, appointed Shi Bin's son Yan as crown prince, Shi Jian as attendant-in-chief, Shi Chong as grand guardian, Shi Bao as grand marshal, Shi Kun as grand general, Shi Min as overseer of all military affairs within and without, grand general who aids the state, recorder of Masters-of-Writing affairs, assisting rule.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Lady Zheng to empress dowager, Lady Zhang to empress, named Shi Yan—Shi Bin's son—heir apparent, Shi Jian palace attendant, Shi Chong grand guardian, Shi Bao grand marshal, Shi Kun commander-in-chief, and Shi Min supreme military overseer, state-aiding grand general, and secretariat regent.

sentences.zh: 暴風拔樹，震雷，雨雹大如盂升。

translations.literal: A violent wind uprooted trees; shaking thunder; hail fell as large as bowls and sheng-measures.
translations.idiomatic: Gales tore up timber, thunder cracked, and hailstones wide as bowls hammered the capital.

sentences.zh: 太武、暉華殿災，諸門觀閣蕩然，其乘輿服御燒者太半，光焰照天，金石皆盡，火月餘乃滅。

translations.literal: Grand Martial and Huihua halls suffered fire disaster; gates, towers, and galleries were swept bare; of imperial carriages and wardrobe those burned were more than half; light and flame illumined heaven; metal and stone were all consumed; the fire after more than a month then died.
translations.idiomatic: Flames gutted the Grand Martial and Huihua halls, stripped gates and belvederes bare, and consumed more than half the chariots and robes—molten metal glared skyward for over a month before the blaze died.

sentences.zh: 雨血周遍鄴城。

translations.literal: Blood rain fell everywhere throughout Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Rain the color of blood drenched every ward of Ye.

sentences.zh: 石沖時鎮于薊，聞遵殺世而自立，乃謂其僚佐曰：「世受先帝之命，遵輒廢殺，罪逆莫大，其敕內外戎嚴，孤將親討之。

translations.literal: Shi Chong at that time was stationed at Ji; hearing Zun had killed Shi and established himself, he said to his staff and aides: "Shi received the late emperor's mandate; Zun abruptly deposed and killed him—the crime of rebellion is greatest; order inner and outer to tighten armor; I myself will personally punish him."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong held Ji when news came that Shi Zun had murdered Shi Shi and seized power; he told his advisers, "The boy bore the late emperor's charge—Shi Zun slew him by treason; seal the passes—I march myself to punish him."

sentences.zh: 」於是留寧北沭堅戍幽州，帥眾五萬，自薊討遵，傳檄燕、趙，所在雲集，比及常山，眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he left northern pacification Mu Jian to garrison Youzhou, led a host of fifty thousand, from Ji punished Zun, transmitted proclamations through Yan and Zhao; wherever they went clouds gathered; by the time they reached Changshan, the host exceeded one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He left Mu Jian of northern pacification to hold Youzhou, took fifty thousand men from Ji, broadcast manifestos across Yan and Zhao until recruits swarmed in—beyond Changshan his army topped a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 次於苑鄉，遇遵赦書，謂左右曰：「吾弟一也，死者不可復追，何為復相殘乎！

translations.literal: He halted at Yuanxiang; encountering Zun's amnesty edict, he said to those at his side: "My younger brother and I are one; the dead cannot be pursued back—why again mutually injure one another!
translations.idiomatic: Camped at Yuanxiang, he read Shi Zun's pardon and mused aloud, "He is still my brother—the dead cannot return; why cut one another down again?

sentences.zh: 吾將歸矣。

translations.literal: I shall return."
translations.idiomatic: I am going home."

sentences.zh: 」其將陳暹進曰：「彭城篡弑自尊，為罪大矣。

translations.literal: " His general Chen Xian advanced saying: "The prince of Pengcheng usurped and murdered to honor himself—the crime is great.
translations.idiomatic: General Chen Xian cut in, "The prince of Pengcheng murdered his way to the throne—the guilt is monstrous.

sentences.zh: 王雖北旆，臣將南轅，平京師，擒彭城，然後奉迎大駕。

translations.literal: Though Your Highness turns the banner north, your servant will turn the axle south, pacify the capital, capture the prince of Pengcheng, then welcome the great chariot."
translations.idiomatic: You may wheel north, my lord, but I will drive south, seize the capital, cage the prince of Pengcheng, and only then escort your majesty home."

sentences.zh: 」沖從之。

translations.literal: " Chong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong agreed.

sentences.zh: 遵馳遣王擢以書喻沖，沖弗聽。

translations.literal: Zun urgently sent Wang Zhuo with a letter to enlighten Chong; Chong did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun raced Wang Zhuo ahead with a letter dissuading Shi Chong, who ignored it.

sentences.zh: 遵假石閔黃鉞、金鉦，與李農等率精卒十萬討之。

translations.literal: Zun lent Shi Min the yellow battle-axe and golden cymbals; together with Li Nong and others he led one hundred thousand elite troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun handed Shi Min the yellow axe and golden bells; with Li Nong and others he marched one hundred thousand picked troops against the rebel.

sentences.zh: 戰于平棘，沖師大敗，獲沖於元氏，賜死，坑其士卒三萬餘人。

translations.literal: They fought at Pingji; Chong's army was greatly defeated; Chong was captured at Yuanshi, granted death, and more than thirty thousand of his soldiers were buried alive in pits.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingji Shi Chong's host shattered; taken at Yuanshi he was forced to kill himself, and thirty thousand of his men were buried alive in mass graves.

sentences.zh: 始葬季龍，號其墓為顯原陵，偽諡武皇帝，廟號太祖。

translations.literal: They began burying Jilong; his tomb was titled Manifest Plain Mound; false posthumous title Martial Emperor; temple name Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: They laid Shi Hu to rest on Manifest Plain tumulus, posthumously dubbing him Martial Emperor with temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 遵揚州刺史王浹以淮南歸順。

translations.literal: Zun's Yangzhou Governor Wang Jie brought Huainan to allegiance in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun's Yangzhou governor Wang Jie delivered Huainan to Jin in submission.

sentences.zh: 晉西中郎將陳逵進據壽春。

translations.literal: Jin's General of the Household for the West Chen Kui advanced and occupied Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kui, Jin's western palace general, marched into Shouchun and seized it.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍褚裒率師伐遵，次於下邳，遵以李農為南討大都督，率騎二萬來距。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Chu Pou led troops against Shi Zun and halted at Xiapi; Zun appointed Li Nong grand commander-in-chief for the southern expedition and sent twenty thousand horsemen to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou, commanding Jin's northern expedition, struck toward Shi Zun and stopped at Xiapi; Zun gave Li Nong the southern front with twenty thousand horse to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 裒不能進，退屯廣陵。

translations.literal: Pou could not advance; he withdrew and encamped at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou failed to push forward and fell back to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 陳逵聞之，懼，遂焚壽春積聚，毀城而還。

translations.literal: When Chen Kui heard this he became afraid; he then burned the accumulated stores at Shouchun, tore down the walls, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kui panicked at the news, torched the Shouchun granaries, demolished the ramparts, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 石苞時鎮長安，謀帥關中之眾攻鄴，左長史石光、司馬曹曜等固諫。

translations.literal: Shi Bao was then stationed at Chang'an and plotted to lead the armies of Guanzhong against Ye; left chief clerk Shi Guang, marshal Cao Yao, and others repeatedly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao held Chang'an and planned to march all Guanzhong on Ye; his chief clerk Shi Guang and marshal Cao Yao pleaded in vain against the venture.

sentences.zh: 苞怒，誅光等百餘人。

translations.literal: Bao grew furious and executed Guang and more than a hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: In his rage Shi Bao put Shi Guang and over a hundred men to the sword.

sentences.zh: 苞性貪而無謀，雍州豪石知其無成，並遣使告晉梁州刺史司馬勳。

translations.literal: Bao was greedy by nature and devoid of strategy; the magnates of Yongzhou knew he would accomplish nothing and jointly sent envoys to inform Jin's governor of Liangzhou, Sima Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao was grasping and witless; Yongzhou's leading families saw no hope in him and messaged Jin's Liangzhou governor Sima Xun.

sentences.zh: 勳於是率眾赴之，壁於懸鉤，去長安二百餘里，使治中劉煥攻京兆太守劉秀離，斬之。

translations.literal: Xun therefore led his forces to join them, fortified at Xuangu over two hundred li from Chang'an, and ordered his aide Liu Huan to attack the governor of Jingzhao, Liu Xiuli, whom he beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xun marched to their aid, dug in at Xuangu two hundred-odd li from Chang'an, and sent Liu Huan against Liu Xiuli of Jingzhao—who lost his head.

sentences.zh: 三輔豪右多殺其令長，擁三十餘壁，有眾五萬以應勳。

translations.literal: Throughout the Three Adjuncts the powerful gentry slew many of their magistrates, held more than thirty fortified camps, and rallied fifty thousand men to answer Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Across the Three Adjuncts notables killed their officials, holed up in thirty-odd stockades, and raised fifty thousand fighters for Sima Xun.

sentences.zh: 苞輟攻鄴之謀，使麻秋、姚國等率騎距勳。

translations.literal: Bao abandoned the plan to strike Ye and ordered Ma Qiu, Yao Guo, and others to lead cavalry against Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao dropped his Ye offensive and sent Ma Qiu and Yao Guo out with mounted troops to meet Sima Xun.

sentences.zh: 遵遣車騎王朗率精騎二萬，以外討勳為名，因劫苞，送之於鄴。

translations.literal: Zun dispatched Wang Lang of the chariot-and-cavalry corps with twenty thousand picked riders; under the pretext of campaigning against Xun abroad he seized Bao and sent him to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun ordered Wang Lang forward with twenty thousand elite horse—ostensibly to fight Sima Xun—only to arrest Shi Bao in transit and haul him to Ye.

sentences.zh: 勳又為朗所距，釋懸鉤，拔宛城，殺遵南陽太守袁景而還。

translations.literal: Xun was again blocked by Lang; he abandoned Xuangu, took Wancheng, executed Yuan Jing, Zun's governor of Nanyang, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang checked Sima Xun again; he quit Xuangu, seized Wancheng, killed Yuan Jing, Shi Zun's prefect of Nanyang, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，遵之發李城也，謂石閔曰：「努力！

translations.literal: At first, when Zun set out from Licheng, he said to Shi Min: "Exert yourself!
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Zun first rode out from Licheng he told Shi Min, "Throw your whole weight behind this.

sentences.zh: 事成，以爾為儲貳。

translations.literal: When the deed is done We shall make you heir apparent."
translations.idiomatic: Succeed, and you will be my heir."

sentences.zh: 」既而立衍，閔甚失望，自以勳高一時，規專朝政，遵忌而不能任。

translations.literal: " Thereafter he enthroned Yan; Min was deeply disappointed. Deeming his own merit unrivaled in the age, he aimed to monopolize court power, while Zun envied him and would not entrust him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he raised Shi Yan instead. Shi Min burned—he alone had turned the tide—and meant to rule the council while Shi Zun mistrusted him and withheld real authority.

sentences.zh: 閔既為都督，總內外兵權，乃懷撫殿中將士及故東宮高力萬餘人，皆奏為殿中員外將軍，爵關外侯，賜以宮女，樹己之恩。

translations.literal: Once Min became commander-in-chief and held all military authority inside and outside the palace, he won over the palace guard and more than ten thousand former eastern-palace Gao Li veterans, memorializing them all as supernumerary generals of the palace hall with noble rank as marquises beyond the passes, granting them palace women to cultivate gratitude toward himself.
translations.idiomatic: As grand commander Shi Min held every blade; he courted the hall troops and ten thousand eastern-palace toughs, had them named supernumerary hall generals and marquises beyond the passes, and showered them with palace women to seal their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 遵弗之猜也，而更題名善惡以挫抑之，眾咸怨矣。

translations.literal: Zun did not suspect him in this; instead he posted lists grading good and evil names to humiliate and suppress them, and everyone harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun never sensed the danger; he published virtue-and-vice rosters to shame them instead, and resentment spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 而又納中書令孟准、左衛將軍王鸞之計，頗疑憚于閔，稍奪兵權。

translations.literal: Moreover he adopted the counsel of secretariat director Meng Zhun and left guard general Wang Luan, grew suspicious and fearful of Min, and gradually stripped away his military authority.
translations.idiomatic: He also listened to Meng Zhun and Wang Luan, turned wary of Shi Min, and slowly peeled away his commands.

sentences.zh: 閔益有恨色，准等咸勸誅之。

translations.literal: Min increasingly showed hatred on his face; Zhun and the rest all urged executing him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min's glare turned murderous; Meng Zhun's faction pressed Shi Zun to kill him.

sentences.zh: 遵召石鑒等入，議于其太后鄭氏之前，皆請誅之。

translations.literal: Zun summoned Shi Jian and others to deliberate before his empress dowager, Lady Zheng; all petitioned to execute Min.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun assembled Shi Jian and the princes before Empress Dowager Zheng; every voice demanded Shi Min's death.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏曰：「李城回師，無棘奴豈有今日！

translations.literal: Lady Zheng said: "When the army turned back at Licheng, without Thorn Slave where would today be!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng answered, "When your host wheeled home from Licheng, without Jinu you would have no throne.

sentences.zh: 小驕縱之，不可便殺也。

translations.literal: He is a little proud—indulge him; you must not kill him outright."
translations.idiomatic: Let his small arrogance pass—you must not cut him down yet."

sentences.zh: 」鑒出，遣宦者楊環馳以告閔，閔遂劫李農及右衛王基，密謀廢遵。

translations.literal: " When Jian left, he sent the eunuch Yang Huan galloping to warn Min; Min then seized Li Nong and Wang Ji of the right guard and secretly plotted to depose Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian slipped out and sent the eunuch Yang Huan racing to alert Shi Min, who kidnapped Li Nong and Wang Ji of the right guard and schemed to oust Shi Zun.

sentences.zh: 使將軍蘇亥、周成率甲士三十執遵于如意觀。

translations.literal: He ordered generals Su Hai and Zhou Cheng to lead thirty armored soldiers and seize Zun at the Ruyi Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: He told Su Hai and Zhou Cheng to take thirty armored men and arrest Shi Zun at the Ruyi belvedere.

sentences.zh: 遵時方與婦人彈棋，問成等曰：「反者誰也？

translations.literal: Zun was at that moment playing pitch-and-roam chess with women; he asked Cheng and the others: "Who rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun was playing pitch-pot with his consorts when they burst in. "Who turns traitor?" he asked.

sentences.zh: 」成曰：「義陽王鑒當立。

translations.literal: " Cheng said: "The Prince of Yiyang, Jian, is to be enthroned."
translations.idiomatic: "The prince of Yiyang, Shi Jian, takes the crown," Zhou Cheng replied.

sentences.zh: 」遵曰：「我尚如是，汝等立鑒，復能幾時！

translations.literal: " Zun said: "Even I am treated thus; when you enthrone Jian, how long can it last!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun laughed bitterly. "If this is my fate, how long will any of you endure Shi Jian?"

sentences.zh: 」乃殺之于琨華殿，誅鄭氏及其太子衍、上光祿張斐、中書令孟准、左衛王鸞等。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they killed him in Kunhua Hall and executed Lady Zheng, his heir Yan, superior household groom Zhang Fei, secretariat director Meng Zhun, Wang Luan of the left guard, and others.
translations.idiomatic: They slew him in Kunhua Hall, then butchered Lady Zheng, Crown Prince Yan, Zhang Fei of the superior household income, Meng Zhun, Wang Luan, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 遵凡在位一百八十三日。

translations.literal: In all Zun occupied the throne one hundred eighty-three days.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zun had ruled one hundred eighty-three days.

sentences.zh: 石鑒

translations.literal: Shi Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: Shi Jian.

sentences.zh: 鑒乃僭位，大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: Jian then usurped the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty short of capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian seized the throne and ordered mercy for all crimes below death.

sentences.zh: 以石閔為大將軍，封武德王，李農為大司馬，並錄尚書事；

translations.literal: He appointed Shi Min grand general and prince of Wude, Li Nong grand minister of war, both with custody of Masters-of-Writing affairs;
translations.idiomatic: He named Shi Min commander-in-chief and prince of Wude, Li Nong minister of war—both controlling the secretariat—

sentences.zh: 郎闓為司空，秦州刺史劉群為尚書左僕射，侍中盧諶為中書監。

translations.literal: Lang Kai minister of works, Liu Qun governor of Qinzhou left vice-director of Masters-of-Writing, attendant Lu Chen supervisor of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: made Lang Kai minister of works, Liu Qun of Qinzhou left vice-director of the secretariat, and palace attendant Lu Chen overseer of the palace writers.

sentences.zh: 鑒使石苞及中書令李松、殿中將軍張才等夜誅閔、農于琨華殿，不克，禁中擾亂。

translations.literal: Jian ordered Shi Bao, secretariat director Li Song, palace-hall general Zhang Cai, and others to assassinate Min and Li Nong by night in Kunhua Hall; they failed, and the forbidden precincts erupted in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian sent Shi Bao, Li Song, and Zhang Cai to murder Shi Min and Li Nong after dark in Kunhua Hall; the bid collapsed and the inner palace exploded into riot.

sentences.zh: 鑒恐閔為變，偽若不知者，夜斬松、才于西中華門，並誅石苞。

translations.literal: Jian feared Min might mutiny; pretending ignorance, he had Song and Cai executed that night at the western Zhonghua Gate and put Shi Bao to death as well.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified of Shi Min's revenge, Shi Jian feigned innocence and that same night killed Li Song and Zhang Cai at the western Zhonghua gate, along with Shi Bao.

sentences.zh: 時石祗在襄國，與姚弋仲、苻洪等通和，連兵檄誅閔、農。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Zhi was at Xiangguo; he had opened talks with Yao Yizhong, Fu Hong, and others, linked armies, and issued proclamations calling for the execution of Min and Li Nong.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi held Xiangguo and had made peace with Yao Yizhong and Fu Hong; their allied hosts broadcast warrants for Shi Min and Li Nong's heads.

sentences.zh: 鑒遣石琨為大都督，與張舉及侍中呼延盛率步騎七萬分討祗等。

translations.literal: Jian dispatched Shi Kun as grand commander-in-chief with Zhang Ju and attendant Huyan Sheng to lead seventy thousand infantry and horse on separate strikes against Zhi and company.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian named Shi Kun supreme commander and sent him with Zhang Ju and Huyan Sheng at the head of seventy thousand foot and horse against Shi Zhi.

sentences.zh: 中領軍石成、侍中石啟、前河東太守石暉謀誅閔、農，閔、農殺之。

translations.literal: Palace-army commander Shi Cheng, attendant Shi Qi, and former Hedong governor Shi Hui plotted to kill Min and Li Nong; Min and Li Nong slew them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cheng, Shi Qi, and ex-prefect Shi Hui of Hedong conspired against Shi Min and Li Nong; the pair struck first and killed them.

sentences.zh: 龍驤孫伏都、劉銖等結羯士三千伏于胡天，亦欲誅閔等。

translations.literal: Sun Fudu and Liu Zhu of the Dragon Raising guard rallied three thousand Jie soldiers in ambush at Hutian, intending likewise to execute Min and his allies.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fudu and Liu Zhu mustered three thousand Jie fighters in hiding at Hutian, aiming to cut down Shi Min.

sentences.zh: 時鑒在中臺，伏都率三十餘人將升臺挾鑒以攻之。

translations.literal: Jian was then at the central terrace; Fudu led more than thirty men intending to ascend the terrace, seize Jian, and turn against Min.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian sat on the central terrace while Sun Fudu rushed thirty followers up the stairs to seize the emperor and wheel on Shi Min.

sentences.zh: 臨見伏都毀閣道，鑒問其故。

translations.literal: Seeing Fudu tear down the elevated walkway, Jian asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Watching Sun Fudu wreck the skywalk, Shi Jian demanded why.

sentences.zh: 伏都曰：「李農等反，巳在東掖門，臣嚴率衛士，謹先啟知。

translations.literal: Fudu said: "Li Nong and the others rebel; they are already at the eastern Ye Gate; your servant sternly leads the guards and respectfully informs you first."
translations.idiomatic: "Li Nong has risen—the eastern Ye gate has fallen; I rally the household guard and came first to report," Sun Fudu said.

sentences.zh: 」鑒曰：「卿是功臣，好為官陳力。

translations.literal: " Jian said: "You are a minister of merit; exert yourself faithfully for the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian answered, "You are a champion—serve the dynasty with everything you have.

sentences.zh: 朕從臺觀卿，勿慮無報也。

translations.literal: We shall watch you from the terrace; do not fear that reward will not come."
translations.idiomatic: I will watch from this height; do not doubt you will be repaid."

sentences.zh: 」於是伏都及銖率眾攻閔、農，不克，屯于鳳陽門。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Fudu and Zhu led their forces against Min and Li Nong, failed, and encamped at Fengyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fudu and Liu Zhu threw their weight at Shi Min and Li Nong, lost, and dug in at Fengyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 閔、農率眾數千毀金明門而入。

translations.literal: Min and Li Nong led several thousand men, smashed the Jinming Gate, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min and Li Nong shattered the Jinming Gate with thousands of fighters and poured through.

sentences.zh: 鑒懼閔之誅己也，馳招閔、農，開門內之，謂曰：「孫伏都反，卿宜速討之。

translations.literal: Jian feared Min would execute him; he galloped to summon Min and Li Nong, opened the gates to admit them, and said: "Sun Fudu rebels; you must hurry to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Certain Shi Min meant to kill him, Shi Jian raced to open the gates: "Sun Fudu rebels—strike him now.

sentences.zh: 」閔、農攻斬伏都等，自鳳陽至琨華，橫屍相枕，流血成渠。

translations.literal: " Min and Li Nong attacked, beheaded Fudu and his party, and from Fengyang to Kunhua corpses lay piled head to heel while blood ran in channels.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min and Li Nong cut Sun Fudu down; from Fengyang to Kunhua the dead lay in windrows and blood pooled in the streets.

sentences.zh: 宣令內外六夷敢稱兵杖者斬之。

translations.literal: They proclaimed that any tribesman who dared bear arms inside or outside would be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: They decreed instant death for any armed northern tribesman within the walls or beyond.

sentences.zh: 胡人或斬關，或逾城而出者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Northerners who hacked the gates or scaled the walls to flee were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Countless men broke the barriers or climbed out over the battlements.

sentences.zh: 使尚書王簡、少府王郁帥眾數千，守鑒於禦龍觀，懸食給之。

translations.literal: They ordered Masters-of-Writing Wang Jian and lesser treasury Wang Yu to command several thousand troops, guard Jian inside the Dragon-Taming Observatory, and lower food to him on ropes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian of the secretariat and Wang Yu of the lesser treasury penned Shi Jian inside the Dragon-Taming belvedere with thousands of men and lowered baskets of food.

sentences.zh: 令城內曰：「與官同心者住，不同心者各任所之。

translations.literal: They commanded within the city: "Those of one mind with the court may stay; those not of one mind may each go where they will.
translations.idiomatic: An order echoed through the wards: stay if you stand with the throne, leave freely if you do not.

sentences.zh: 」敕城門不復相禁。

translations.literal: " They ordered the gates no longer mutually barred.
translations.idiomatic: The gates were commanded open and none barred the roads.

sentences.zh: 於是趙人百里內悉入城，胡羯去者填門。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhao commoners within a hundred li all entered the city, while departing Hu and Jie clogged the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao townsfolk for a hundred li flooded inward as Jie and Hu streamed out until every gate jammed.

sentences.zh: 閔知胡之不為己用也，班令內外趙人，斬一胡首送鳳陽門者，文官進位三等，武職悉拜牙門。

translations.literal: Min knew the northerners would not serve him; he issued an edict to Zhao people inside and outside that whoever delivered one northern tribesman's head to Fengyang Gate would advance three grades as a civil official, while military officers would all be commissioned as gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the tribes would never obey, Shi Min promised three civil promotions—or a gate-captain's commission—to any Zhao who brought a tribesman's head to Fengyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 一日之中，斬首數萬。

translations.literal: In a single day tens of thousands of heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: That one day saw tens of thousands slain.

sentences.zh: 閔躬率趙人誅諸胡羯，無貴賤男女少長皆斬之，死者二十餘萬，屍諸城外，悉為野犬豺狼所食。

translations.literal: Min personally led Zhao people in slaughtering every Hu and Jie; without regard to noble or base, male or female, young or old, all were beheaded—more than two hundred thousand dead whose corpses were piled beyond the walls until wild dogs and wolves devoured them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min himself led the Zhao in butchering every Jie and Hu—rich or poor, young or old—until two hundred thousand corpses littered the plain outside Ye for curs and wolves to tear apart.

sentences.zh: 屯據四方者，所在承閔書誅之，于時高鼻多須至有濫死者半。

translations.literal: Garrisons holding the four quarters, wherever they received Min's document, executed targets accordingly; at that time those with high noses and heavy beards were slain indiscriminately until perhaps half died wrongfully.
translations.idiomatic: Outlying commands acted on Shi Min's writ and killed on sight—so many tall-nosed, bearded men fell by mistake that innocents may have matched the guilty.

sentences.zh: 太宰趙鹿、太尉張舉、中軍張春、光祿石嶽、撫軍石甯、武衛張季及諸公侯、卿、校、龍騰等萬餘人出奔襄國。
