translations.literal: Grand steward Zhao Lu, grand commandant Zhang Ju, central army Zhang Chun, household groom Shi Yue, pacification general Shi Ning, martial guard Zhang Ji, together with various dukes, marquises, ministers, colonels, Dragon Surge officers, and others—more than ten thousand—fled toward Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten thousand grandees—Zhao Lu, Zhang Ju, Zhang Chun, Shi Yue, Shi Ning, Zhang Ji, and Dragon Surge commanders—bolted for Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 石琨奔據冀州，撫軍張沈屯滏口，張賀度據石瀆，建義段勤據黎陽，甯南楊群屯桑壁，劉國據陽城，段龕據陳留，姚弋仲據混橋，苻洪據枋頭，眾各數萬。

translations.literal: Shi Kun fled to hold Jizhou; pacification general Zhang Shen encamped at Fukou; Zhang Heduo held Shidu; Duan Qin the righteous-establishment general held Liyang; Yang Qun of southern pacification encamped at Sangbi; Liu Guo held Yangcheng; Duan Kan held Chenliu; Yao Yizhong held Hunqiao; Fu Hong held Fangtou—each with armies numbering several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun seized Jizhou while Zhang Shen held Fukou, Zhang Heduo Shidu, Duan Qin Liyang, Yang Qun Sangbi, Liu Guo Yangcheng, Duan Kan Chenliu, Yao Yizhong Hunqiao, and Fu Hong Fangtou—each commanding tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 王朗、麻秋自長安奔於洛陽。

translations.literal: Wang Lang and Ma Qiu fled from Chang'an to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang and Ma Qiu raced from Chang'an to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 秋承閔書，誅朗部胡千餘。

translations.literal: Qiu acting on Min's document executed more than a thousand Hu in Lang's command.
translations.idiomatic: On Shi Min's orders Ma Qiu slaughtered over a thousand tribesmen under Wang Lang.

sentences.zh: 朗奔于襄國。

translations.literal: Lang fled to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang fled to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 麻秋率眾奔于苻洪。

translations.literal: Ma Qiu led his host and fled to Fu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu defected to Fu Hong with his troops.

sentences.zh: 石琨及張舉、王朗率眾七萬伐鄴，石閔率騎千餘，距之城北。

translations.literal: Shi Kun together with Zhang Ju and Wang Lang led seventy thousand troops against Ye; Shi Min led more than a thousand riders and opposed them north of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun, Zhang Ju, and Wang Lang brought seventy thousand men against Ye; Shi Min met them beyond the north wall with a thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 閔執兩刃矛，馳騎擊之，皆應鋒摧潰，斬級三千。

translations.literal: Min wielded a double-bladed spear, galloped among them, and shattered every line he touched, taking three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: He charged with a twin-edged lance and rode through their ranks as if they were straw, claiming three thousand kills.

sentences.zh: 琨等大敗，遂歸於冀州。

translations.literal: Kun and the others were utterly defeated and withdrew into Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun's coalition broke and crawled back to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 閔與李農率騎三萬討張賀度于石瀆，鑒密遣宦者齎書召張沈等，使承虛襲鄴。

translations.literal: Min with Li Nong led thirty thousand riders against Zhang Heduo at Shidu; Jian secretly sent eunuchs with letters summoning Zhang Shen and others to exploit the emptiness and raid Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min and Li Nong marched thirty thousand horse on Zhang Heduo at Shidu while Shi Jian secretly dispatched eunuchs urging Zhang Shen to strike undefended Ye.

sentences.zh: 宦者以告閔、農，閔、農馳還，廢鑒殺之，誅季龍孫三十八人，盡殪石氏。

translations.literal: The eunuchs informed Min and Li Nong; Min and Li Nong galloped back, deposed Jian and killed him, executed thirty-eight grandsons of Jilong, and utterly extinguished the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs betrayed the plot; Shi Min and Li Nong wheeled home, deposed and executed Shi Jian, slew thirty-eight of Shi Hu's grandsons, and erased the Shi house.

sentences.zh: 鑒在位一百三日。

translations.literal: Jian occupied the throne one hundred three days.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jian had reigned one hundred three days.

sentences.zh: 季龍小男混，將妻妾數人奔京師，敕收付廷尉，俄而斬之于建康市。

translations.literal: Jilong's youngest son Hun fled to the capital with several wives and concubines; an edict ordered him seized and handed to the minister of justice; shortly he was beheaded in Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu's youngest, Shi Hun, reached the Jin court with a handful of women; the emperor jailed him and soon struck off his head in Jiankang's marketplace.

sentences.zh: 季龍十三子，五人為冉閔所殺，八人自相殘害，混至此又死。

translations.literal: Of Jilong's thirteen sons, five were killed by Ran Min, eight destroyed one another, and Hun likewise died upon reaching this point.
translations.idiomatic: Of Shi Hu's thirteen sons five fell to Ran Min, eight slew each other, and Shi Hun died last at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 初，讖言滅石者陵，尋而石閔徙蘭陵公，季龍惡之，改蘭陵為武興郡，至是終為閔所滅。

translations.literal: Earlier a prophecy said "ling" would destroy the Shi; soon Shi Min was moved to prince of Lanling; Jilong detested this and renamed Lanling commandery Wuxing; reaching this point they were finally extinguished by Min.
translations.idiomatic: A rumor once named "ling" as the doom of Shi—then Shi Min became prince of Lanling, so Shi Hu renamed the district Wuxing in superstition—yet Ran Min ended the clan all the same.

sentences.zh: 始勒以成帝僭立，二主四子，凡二十三年，以穆帝滅。

translations.literal: From the time Shi Le usurped under Emperor Cheng through two rulers and four sons—twenty-three years in all—they were destroyed under Emperor Mu.
translations.idiomatic: From Shi Le's seizure of power under Cheng-di through two emperors and four heirs stretched twenty-three years of Zhao rule until Mu-di watched it vanish.

sentences.zh: 石閔

translations.literal: Shi Min.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: Shi Min.

sentences.zh: 〈冉閔〉

translations.literal: 〈Ran Min〉
translations.idiomatic: Alternate name: Ran Min.

sentences.zh: 閔字永曾，小字棘奴，季龍之養孫也。

translations.literal: Min's style name was Yongzeng; his childhood name Thorn Slave; he was Jilong's adopted grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min, courtesy Yongzeng and childhood name Jinu, was Shi Hu's adopted grandson.

sentences.zh: 父瞻，字弘武，本姓冉，名良，魏郡內黃人也。

translations.literal: His father Zhan, style Hongwu, originally bore the surname Ran and the personal name Liang; he was a man of Neihuang in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ran Zhan (Hongwu), born Ran Liang of Neihuang in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先漢黎陽騎都督，累世牙門。

translations.literal: His ancestors had been Han-era cavalry directors at Liyang; for generations they served as gate captains.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served Han as Liyang cavalry directors for generations of gate-captain posts.

sentences.zh: 勒破陳午，獲瞻，時年十二，命季龍子之。

translations.literal: When Le defeated Chen Wu he captured Zhan, then twelve years old, and ordered Jilong to adopt him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le broke Chen Wu he seized the twelve-year-old boy and told Shi Hu to adopt him.

sentences.zh: 驍猛多力，攻戰無前。

translations.literal: He was fierce, brave, and immensely strong; in attack none stood before him.
translations.idiomatic: He fought like a demon—strong, relentless, and always in the van.

sentences.zh: 歷位左積射將軍、西華侯。

translations.literal: He rose through the posts of general of the left for stacked volleys and marquis of Xihua.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed to left rapid-crossbow general and marquis of Xihua.

sentences.zh: 閔幼而果銳，季龍撫之如孫。

translations.literal: Min was decisive and keen even as a boy; Jilong cherished him as a grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he was bold and sharp; Shi Hu pampered him like blood kin.

sentences.zh: 及長，身長八尺，善謀策，勇力絕人。

translations.literal: When grown he stood eight chi tall, excelled in stratagem, and his courage and strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Full grown at eight chi, he was cunning in counsel and unmatched in raw valor.

sentences.zh: 拜建節將軍，徙封修成侯，歷位北中郎將、遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed general who establishes the standard, transferred to marquis of Xiucheng, and served as northern palace general and roaming-strike general.
translations.idiomatic: He became general of the established standard, then marquis of Xiucheng, and held northern palace general and roaming-strike commands.

sentences.zh: 季龍之敗于昌黎，閔軍獨全，由此功名大顯。

translations.literal: When Jilong was defeated at Changli, Min's army alone remained intact; from this his merit and fame rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu lost at Changli only Shi Min's corps marched home whole—and his legend ignited.

sentences.zh: 及敗梁犢之後，威聲彌振，胡夏宿將莫不憚之。

translations.literal: After he defeated Liang Du his dread reputation spread further; veteran generals of Hu and Xia lands none did not fear him.
translations.idiomatic: After he shattered Liang Du his name shook north and south; every old soldier dreaded him.

sentences.zh: ，殺石鑒，其司徒申鐘、司空郎闓等四十八人上尊號于閔，閔固讓李農，農以死固請，於是僭即皇帝位於南郊，大赦，改元曰永興，國號大魏，復姓冉氏。

translations.literal: , killed Shi Jian; forty-eight men including his minister of education Shen Zhong and minister of works Lang Kai offered Min the supreme title; Min firmly yielded to Li Nong; Li Nong begged with his life; thereupon Min usurped the emperor's position at the southern suburb, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Yongxing, styled the state Great Wei, and restored the surname Ran.
translations.idiomatic: Having killed Shi Jian, forty-eight ministers led by Shen Zhong and Lang Kai pressed the throne on him; he thrust it at Li Nong until Li Nong pleaded with his life that Min accept. At the southern altar he proclaimed himself emperor of Great Wei, adopted Yongxing, restored the surname Ran, and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 追尊其祖隆元皇帝，考瞻烈祖高皇帝，尊母王氏為皇太后，立妻董氏為皇后，子智為皇太子。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his grandfather Long as Emperor Yuan, his father Zhan as Emperor Gaodi with temple name Liezu, elevated Lady Wang as empress dowager, invested Lady Dong as empress, and named his son Zhi heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He canonized his grandfather as Yuan emperor, his father Ran Zhan as martyr-king Gaodi, raised Lady Wang to empress dowager, Lady Dong to empress, and named Ran Zhi crown prince.

sentences.zh: 以李農為太宰、領太尉、錄尚書事，封齊王，農諸子皆封為縣公。

translations.literal: He appointed Li Nong grand steward with concurrent grand commandant and custody of Masters-of-Writing affairs, enfeoffed him prince of Qi, and enfeoffed Li Nong's sons as district dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nong became grand tutor with the minister of war's portfolio and secretariat control, prince of Qi, while each of his sons took a district duchy.

sentences.zh: 封其子胤、明、裕皆為王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed his sons Yin, Ming, and Yu all as princes.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yin, Ming, and Yu were all created princes.

sentences.zh: 文武進位三等，封爵有差。

translations.literal: Civil and military officers advanced three grades in rank; noble titles were granted according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and martial ranks rose three steps; titles landed according to desert.

sentences.zh: 遣使者持節赦諸屯結，皆不從。

translations.literal: He dispatched envoys bearing credentials to offer amnesty to the various entrenched camps; none obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Staff-bearing envoys carried pardons to every rebel camp; all refused.

sentences.zh: 石祗聞鑒死，僭稱尊號于襄國，諸六夷據州郡擁兵者皆應之。

translations.literal: When Shi Zhi heard that Jian was dead, he usurped the supreme title at Xiangguo; every tribal leader holding a province or commandery with troops responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Shi Jian's death, Shi Zhi crowned himself at Xiangguo, and every tribal warlord with a seal rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 閔遣使臨江告晉曰：「胡逆亂中原，今已誅之。

translations.literal: Min sent an envoy to the riverbank to inform Jin: "The northern tribes rebelled and threw the Central Plain into chaos; now We have executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min sent a messenger to the Yangzi shore to tell Jin, "The nomads tore the heartland apart—we have slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 若能共討者，可遣軍來也。

translations.literal: If you can join Us in punishing them, you may dispatch armies."
translations.idiomatic: March with us if you dare—send your armies."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷不答。

translations.literal: " The court made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court answered nothing.

sentences.zh: 閔誅李農及其三子，並尚書令王謨、侍中王衍、中常侍嚴震、趙升等。

translations.literal: Min executed Li Nong and his three sons, together with Masters-of-Writing director Wang Mo, attendant Wang Yan, palace attendant Yan Zhen, Zhao Sheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Min killed Li Nong, his three sons, chief secretary Wang Mo, attendant Wang Yan, eunuchs Yan Zhen and Zhao Sheng, and their circle.

sentences.zh: 晉盧江太守袁真攻其合肥，執南蠻校尉桑坦，遷其百姓而還。

translations.literal: Jin's governor of Lujiang, Yuan Zhen, attacked Hefei, captured southern tribes colonel Sang Tan, and relocated the populace before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen, Jin's prefect of Lujiang, struck Hefei, took southern frontier colonel Sang Tan prisoner, and marched the people home.

sentences.zh: 石祗遣其相國石琨率眾十萬伐鄴，進據邯鄲。

translations.literal: Shi Zhi dispatched his minister of state Shi Kun to lead one hundred thousand troops against Ye and advanced to occupy Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi sent his minister Shi Kun with a hundred thousand men against Ye and seized Handan.

sentences.zh: 祗鎮南劉國自繁陽會琨。

translations.literal: Shi Zhi's defender of the south Liu Guo came from Fanyang to join Liu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi's southern commander Liu Guo marched up from Fanyang to rendezvous with Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 閔大敗琨于邯鄲，死者萬餘。

translations.literal: Ran Min greatly defeated Liu Kun at Handan; the dead exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At Handan Ran Min shattered Liu Kun's army, leaving more than ten thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 劉國還屯繁陽。

translations.literal: Liu Guo returned and encamped at Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guo withdrew his camps to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 苻健自枋頭入關。

translations.literal: Fu Jian from Fangtou entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian led his followers from Fangtou into the Guanzhong passes.

sentences.zh: 張賀度、段勤與劉國、靳豚會於昌城，將攻鄴。

translations.literal: Zhang Hedeng and Duan Qin joined Liu Guo and Jin Tun at Changcheng; they intended to strike Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hedeng and Duan Qin concentrated Liu Guo and Jin Tun at Changcheng for an advance on Ye.

sentences.zh: 閔遣尚書左僕射劉群為行臺都督，使其將王泰、崔通、周成等帥步騎十二萬次於黃城，閔躬統精卒八萬繼之，戰於蒼亭。

translations.literal: Ran Min dispatched left vice-director of Masters-of-Book Liu Qun as commander-in-chief of the mobile headquarters, ordered his generals Wang Tai, Cui Tong, Zhou Cheng and others to lead one hundred twenty thousand foot and horse and halt at Huangcheng, Ran Min personally commanded eighty thousand picked troops to follow, and they fought at Cangting.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min put Liu Qun, left vice-director of the secretariat, in charge of the field headquarters and sent Wang Tai, Cui Tong, and Zhou Cheng ahead with a hundred twenty thousand mixed troops to Huangcheng; he followed with eighty thousand elites and offered battle at Cangting.

sentences.zh: 賀度等大敗，死者二萬八千，追斬勒豚于陰安鄉，盡俘其眾，振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Hedeng and the others were greatly defeated; twenty-eight thousand died; they pursued and beheaded Jin Tun at Yin'an township, wholly captured their host, shook the troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hedeng's coalition collapsed with twenty-eight thousand casualties; Ran Min ran Jin Tun down at Yin'an, bagged the army, and marched home in order.

sentences.zh: 戎卒三十餘萬，旌旗鐘鼓綿亙百餘里，雖石氏之盛無以過之。

translations.literal: Martial troops exceeded three hundred thousand; banners, bells, and drums stretched more than a hundred li—even at the height of the Shi clan nothing surpassed this.
translations.idiomatic: Over three hundred thousand soldiers with banners and drums lined a hundred li of road—a display even Shi Zhao's zenith had never matched.

sentences.zh: 閔至自蒼亭，行飲至之禮，清定九流，准才授任，儒學後門多蒙顯進，于時翕然，方之為魏晉之初。

translations.literal: Ran Min arrived from Cangting, performed the post-victory drinking rite, clarified and settled the nine ranks, granted posts according to talent; Confucian scholars from humble households mostly won conspicuous promotion—at the time opinion united in comparing the moment to the beginning of Wei and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Cangting Ran Min held the victory feast, regularized the nine-grade bureaucracy, matched talent to office, and elevated poor scholars—observers likened the mood to the fresh order of early Wei-Jin.

sentences.zh: 閔率步騎十萬攻石祗于襄國，署其子太原王胤為大單于、驃騎大將軍，以降胡一千配為麾下。

translations.literal: Ran Min led one hundred thousand foot and horse to attack Shi Zhi at Xiangguo, appointed his son Prince of Taiyuan Yin grand chanyu and chief agile cavalry general, and assigned one thousand surrendered Hu under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min invested Xiangguo with a hundred thousand troops, named Prince Yin of Taiyuan grand chanyu and chief of agile cavalry, and attached a thousand surrendered Hu fighters to his staff.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫韋謏啟諫甚切，閔覽之大怒，誅謏及其子孫。

translations.literal: Supernumerary palace gentleman Wei Xiao submitted a remonstrance that was very cutting; Ran Min read it and was greatly angry; he executed Xiao and his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao remonstrated bluntly in memorial; Ran Min read it, exploded in rage, and extirpated his line.

sentences.zh: 閔攻襄國百餘日，為土山地道，築室反耕。

translations.literal: Ran Min attacked Xiangguo over a hundred days; he built earthen hills and covered ways, erected shelters and turned the soil as if to farm.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a hundred days Ran Min besieged Xiangguo with siege mounds, tunnels, and huts, signaling a war of attrition.

sentences.zh: 祗大懼，去皇帝之號，稱趙王，遣使詣慕容俊、姚弋仲以乞師。

translations.literal: Zhi was greatly afraid; he cast off the emperor's title, styled himself king of Zhao, and sent envoys to Murong Jun and Yao Yizhong to beg for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Panicked, Shi Zhi dropped his imperial claim, called himself Zhao prince, and implored Murong Jun and Yao Yizhong for relief armies.

sentences.zh: 會石琨自冀州援祗，弋仲復遣其子襄率騎三萬八千至自滆頭，俊遣將軍悅綰率甲卒三萬自龍城，三方勁卒合十餘萬。

translations.literal: When Shi Kun came from Jizhou to aid Zhi, Yizhong again sent his son Xiang with thirty-eight thousand cavalry from Ge Ford, and Jun sent general Yue Wan with thirty thousand armored troops from Longcheng; the three hosts combined to more than one hundred thousand crack soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kun marched from Jizhou to Shi Zhi's aid while Yao Yizhong sent Yao Xiang with thirty-eight thousand riders from Ge Ford and Murong Jun sent Yue Wan with thirty thousand armored men from Longcheng—well over a hundred thousand veterans converged.

sentences.zh: 閔遣車騎胡睦距襄下場長蘆，將軍孫威候琨于黃丘，皆為敵所敗，士卒略盡，睦、威單騎而還。

translations.literal: Ran Min dispatched chariot-and-cavalry Hu Mu to block Yao Xiang below Changlu in the paddock, and general Sun Wei to await Kun at Huangqiu; both were defeated by the enemy, their troops nearly exhausted, and Mu and Wei returned alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Mu failed to stop Yao Xiang near Changlu and Sun Wei failed against Shi Kun at Huangqiu—both units were shredded and the generals rode back alone.

sentences.zh: 琨等軍且至，閔將出擊之，衛將軍王泰諫曰：「窮寇固迷，希望外援。

translations.literal: Kun's army was about to arrive; Ran Min was going to go out and strike them; guard-general Wang Tai remonstrated, saying, "Cornered bandits are sure to cling to delusion and hope for outside rescue.
translations.idiomatic: As Shi Kun closed in Ran Min prepared to sally; guard-general Wang Tai urged, "Besieged foes will cling to fantasy and outside rescue.

sentences.zh: 今強救雲集，欲吾出戰，腹背擊我。

translations.literal: Now strong relief hosts gather like clouds; they want us to come out and fight so they can strike us front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Relief columns are massing to lure us out and hit us from both sides.

sentences.zh: 宜固壘勿出，觀勢而動，以挫其謀。

translations.literal: We ought to hold the ramparts and not emerge, watch how matters shift, and move so as to break their design.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the walls, read the field, and move only to frustrate their plan.

sentences.zh: 今陛下親戎，如失萬全，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty personally bears arms; if we forfeit perfect safety, the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty takes the field and anything goes wrong, the whole venture collapses.

sentences.zh: 請慎無出，臣請率諸將為陛下滅之。

translations.literal: I beg you not to venture out; your servant asks to lead the generals and destroy them for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Stay inside—I will lead the commanders and finish them for you.

sentences.zh: 」閔將從之，道士法饒進曰：「太白經昴，當殺胡王，一戰百克，不可失也。

translations.literal: " Ran Min was about to consent when the Daoist Fa Rao stepped forward and said, "The White Planet has crossed the Mao asterism—this means the Hu king must die; one battle wins all—do not miss it.
translations.idiomatic: " Ran Min nearly agreed until Daoist Fa Rao insisted the White Planet over Mao doomed the Hu ruler and promised total victory in a single clash.

sentences.zh: 」閔攘袂大言曰：「吾戰決矣，敢諫者斬！

translations.literal: " Ran Min threw back his sleeves and declared loudly, "My mind is fixed on battle; whoever remonstrates shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: " Ran Min rolled up his sleeves and roared that the fight was settled and advisors would die.

sentences.zh: 」於是盡眾出戰。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he brought the whole host out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: " He then hurled every man into the open field.

sentences.zh: 姚襄、悅綰、石琨等三面攻之，祗沖其後，閔師大敗。

translations.literal: Yao Xiang, Yue Wan, Shi Kun and others attacked from three sides while Zhi struck their rear; Ran Min's army was catastrophically defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang, Yue Wan, and Shi Kun closed from three sides while Shi Zhi drove into Ran Min's rear—his army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 閔潛于襄國行宮，與十餘騎奔鄴。

translations.literal: Ran Min hid in the traveling palace at Xiangguo and, with a dozen-odd riders, fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min slipped into the Xiangguo lodge and bolted for Ye with barely a dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 降胡栗特康等執冉胤及左僕射劉琦等送於祗，盡殺之。

translations.literal: The surrendered Hu Sogdian Kang and others seized Ran Yin and left vice-director Liu Qi and others, delivered them to Zhi, and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered Hu led by the Sogdian Kang seized Ran Yin and vice-director Liu Qi, handed them to Shi Zhi, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 司空石璞、尚書令徐機、車騎胡睦、侍中李琳、中書監盧諶、少府王郁、尚書劉欽、劉休等諸將士死者十餘萬人，於是人物殲矣。

translations.literal: Minister of works Shi Pu, Masters-of-Book chief Xu Ji, chariot-and-cavalry Hu Mu, attendant Li Lin, palace secretariat overseer Lu Chen, chamberlain for the palace treasury Wang Yu, Masters-of-Book Liu Qin and Liu Xiu and other officers and soldiers who died numbered more than one hundred thousand—talent and materiel were wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, Xu Ji, Hu Mu, Lu Chen, and hosts of ministers and generals fell—over a hundred thousand dead—and Ran Min's regime lost its backbone.

sentences.zh: 賊盜蜂起，司、冀大饑，人相食。

translations.literal: Bandits sprang up like wasps; Si and Ji suffered great famine; people devoured one another.
translations.idiomatic: Brigands swarmed; Si and Ji starved until cannibalism spread.

sentences.zh: 自季龍末年而閔盡散倉庫以樹私恩。

translations.literal: From the last years of Shi Hu, Ran Min had emptied the granaries to buy private loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Shi Hu's twilight Ran Min had drained the treasuries to purchase favor.

sentences.zh: 與羌胡相攻，無月不戰。

translations.literal: He fought Qiang and Hu month after month without pause.
translations.idiomatic: War against Qiang and Hu fronts never paused.

sentences.zh: 青、雍、幽、荊州徙戶及諸氐、羌、胡、蠻數百餘萬，各還本土，道路交錯，互相殺掠，且饑疫死亡，其能達者十有二三。

translations.literal: Several million relocated households from Qing, Yong, You, and Jingzhou together with Di, Qiang, Hu, and Man peoples started homeward in every direction; routes crossed, they slaughtered and robbed one another, hunger and plague carried most off, and only two or three in ten reached safety.
translations.idiomatic: Millions of uprooted Han and non-Han peoples crossed paths heading home, killing and looting amid famine and pestilence—fewer than a third survived the trek.

sentences.zh: 諸夏紛亂，無復農者。

translations.literal: The central lands fell into chaos; no farmers remained.
translations.idiomatic: Heartland agriculture ceased in the general turmoil.

sentences.zh: 閔悔之，誅法饒父子，支解之，贈韋謏大司徒。

translations.literal: Ran Min regretted it; he executed Fa Rao and his son, cut them limb from limb, and posthumously honored Wei Xiao as grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min repented, dismembered Fa Rao and his son, and posthumously raised Wei Xiao to grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 石祗使劉顯帥眾七萬攻鄴。

translations.literal: Shi Zhi sent Liu Xian leading seventy thousand men to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi ordered Liu Xian against Ye with seventy thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 時閔潛還，莫有知者，內外凶凶，皆謂閔已沒矣。

translations.literal: At that time Ran Min had secretly returned and nobody knew; court and camp alike panicked, all believing Ran Min had already perished.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min had sneaked back unseen; rumor spread that he was dead and dread seized everyone.

sentences.zh: 射聲校尉張艾勸閔親郊，以安眾心，閔從之，訛言乃止。

translations.literal: Colonel of archers who shoot by sound Zhang Ai urged Ran Min to perform the suburban sacrifice in person to steady morale; Ran Min followed him and the false tales ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ai persuaded Ran Min to lead a suburban rite to calm the troops; he agreed and the rumors died.

sentences.zh: 劉顯次於明光宮，去鄴二十三里，閔懼，召衛將軍王泰議之。

translations.literal: Liu Xian halted at Mingguang Palace, twenty-three li from Ye; Ran Min was afraid and summoned guard-general Wang Tai to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian camped twenty-three li out at Mingguang Palace; a frightened Ran Min called Wang Tai to council.

sentences.zh: 泰恚其謀之不從，辭以瘡甚。

translations.literal: Tai resented that Ran Min had not followed his plan and pleaded severe sores as excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tai still smarted over the ignored advice and claimed bleeding wounds.

sentences.zh: 閔親臨問之，固稱疾篤。

translations.literal: Ran Min visited him in person to inquire; he insisted his illness was grave.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min went to his bedside; Wang Tai swore he was dying.

sentences.zh: 閔怒，還宮，顧謂左右曰：「巴奴，乃公豈假汝為命邪！

translations.literal: Ran Min grew angry, returned to the palace, and said to those beside him, "Ba slaves—does your lord need you to grant him life!
translations.idiomatic: Furious back at court Ran Min sneered that "Ba" lackeys would not dictate his fate.

sentences.zh: 要將先滅群胡，卻斬王泰。

translations.literal: I mean first to wipe out the Hu hordes, then behead Wang Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He vowed to butcher the Hu first and take Wang Tai's head next.

sentences.zh: 」於是盡眾而戰，大敗顯軍，追奔及于陽平，斬首三萬餘級。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he committed the whole host; he routed Liu Xian's army, chased them to Yangping, and took more than thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: " He threw full strength into the fight, shattered Liu Xian at Yangping, and piled thirty thousand skulls.

sentences.zh: 顯懼，密使請降，求殺祗為效，閔振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Xian was afraid; he secretly sent envoys offering surrender and begged to kill Zhi to prove loyalty; Ran Min shook the troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian sued for peace in secret, offered to murder Shi Zhi as earnest, and Ran Min marched home.

sentences.zh: 會有告王泰招集秦人，將奔關中，閔怒，誅泰，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Meanwhile someone reported that Wang Tai was rallying Qin men intending to flee into Guanzhong; Ran Min was angry, executed Tai, and extirpated his three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that Wang Tai was collecting Qin followers for a dash to Guanzhong; Ran Min executed him and annihilated his kin.

sentences.zh: 劉顯果殺祗及其太宰趙鹿等十餘人，傳首於鄴，送質請命。

translations.literal: Liu Xian indeed killed Zhi together with grand tutor Zhao Lu and more than ten others, sent the heads to Ye, and forwarded hostages begging orders.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian slew Shi Zhi, Zhao Lu, and a dozen courtiers, boxed the heads to Ye, and sent pledges for mercy.

sentences.zh: 驃騎石甯奔于柏人。

translations.literal: Chief agile cavalry Shi Ning fled to Bairen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ning, chief of agile cavalry, bolted to Bairen.

sentences.zh: 閔命焚祗首於通衢。

translations.literal: Ran Min ordered Shi Zhi's head burned at a crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min had Shi Zhi's head burnt in the public way.

sentences.zh: 閔徐州刺史劉啟以鄄城歸順。

translations.literal: Ran Min's Xuzhou governor Liu Qi surrendered Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi, Ran Min's Xuzhou governor, yielded Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 劉顯復率眾伐鄴，閔擊敗之。

translations.literal: Liu Xian again led a host against Ye; Ran Min defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian struck Ye again and Ran Min turned him back.

sentences.zh: 還，稱號于襄國。

translations.literal: He returned and assumed title at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to Xiangguo and reclaimed imperial style there.

sentences.zh: 閔徐州刺史周成、兗州刺史魏統、豫州牧冉遇、荊州刺史樂弘皆以城歸順。

translations.literal: Ran Min's Xuzhou governor Zhou Cheng, Yanzhou governor Wei Tong, Yuzhou shepherd Ran Yu, and Jingzhou governor Yue Hong all surrendered their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Cheng, Wei Tong, Ran Yu, and Yue Hong—Ran Min's regional governors—handed over their walls.

sentences.zh: 平南高崇、征虜呂護執洛州刺史鄭系，以三河歸順。

translations.literal: Pacifier of the south Gao Chong and general who subdues barbarians Lu Hu seized Luozhou governor Zheng Xi and brought the Three Rivers region over.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chong and Lu Hu captured Zheng Xi and submitted the Three Rivers.

sentences.zh: 慕容彪攻陷中山，殺閔甯北白同、幽州刺史劉准，降于慕容俊。

translations.literal: Murong Biao took Zhongshan, killed Ran Min's defender of the north Bai Tong and Youzhou governor Liu Zhun, and yielded to Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Biao seized Zhongshan, executed Bai Tong and Liu Zhun, and went over to Murong Jun.

sentences.zh: 時有雲黃赤色，起東北，長百餘丈，一白鳥從雲間西南去，占者惡之。

translations.literal: At the time there appeared yellow-red clouds rising in the northeast stretching more than a hundred zhang; a white bird flew southwest through them—diviners counted it an evil omen.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow-red vapors a hundred zhang long lifted from the northeast while a white bird cut southwest through them—soothsayers read disaster.

sentences.zh: 劉顯率眾伐常山，太守蘇亥告難於閔。

translations.literal: Liu Xian led a host against Changshan; prefect Su Hai appealed to Ran Min for aid.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian marched on Changshan; Su Hai begged Ran Min for rescue.

sentences.zh: 閔留其大將軍蔣幹等輔其太子智守鄴，親率騎八千救之。

translations.literal: Ran Min left grand general Jiang Gan and others to assist crown prince Zhi in holding Ye and personally led eight thousand cavalry to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: He left Jiang Gan to steady Crown Prince Zhi in Ye and rode to the rescue with eight thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 顯所署大司馬、清河王甯以棗強降于閔，收其餘眾，擊顯，敗之，追奔及于襄國。

translations.literal: The grand marshal whom Xian had appointed, Prince of Qinghe Ning, surrendered Zaoyang to Ran Min; Ran Min gathered the survivors, struck Xian, defeated him, and chased him to Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ning of Qinghe, Liu Xian's grand marshal, defected at Zaoyang; Ran Min rallied the remainder, crushed Liu Xian, and pursued him to Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 顯大將曹伏駒開門為應，遂入襄國，誅顯及其公卿已下百餘人，焚襄國宮室，遷其百姓于鄴。

translations.literal: Xian's general Cao Fuju opened the gates in collusion; they entered Xiangguo, executed Xian and more than one hundred dukes and ministers below him, burned the palace compounds, and moved the common people to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fuju betrayed the walls; Ran Min stormed Xiangguo, slew Liu Xian and his hundred-plus officials, torched the palaces, and shipped the populace to Ye.

sentences.zh: 顯領軍范路率眾千餘，斬關奔於枋頭。

translations.literal: Xian's army director Fan Lu led over a thousand men, broke through the barrier, and fled to Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: Army director Fan Lu hacked through the passes with a thousand followers and raced to Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 時慕容俊已克幽、薊，略地至於冀州。

translations.literal: By then Murong Jun had taken You and Ji and his advance reached Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun already held You and Ji and was probing into Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 閔帥騎距之，與慕容恪相遇于魏昌城。

translations.literal: Ran Min led cavalry to block him and met Murong Ke at Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Min moved horse to intercept and encountered Murong Ke at Weichang.

sentences.zh: 閔大將軍董閏、車騎張溫言于閔曰：「鮮卑乘勝氣勁，不可當也，請避之以溢其氣，然後濟師以擊之，可以捷也。

translations.literal: Ran Min's grand general Dong Run and chariot-and-cavalry Zhang Wen told Ran Min, "The Xianbei ride the momentum of victory and their vigor is unstoppable; we cannot withstand them—please avoid them to bleed their spirit, then raise fresh troops and strike; we can win.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Run and Zhang Wen warned that triumphant Xianbei could not be met head-on and urged Ran Min to sidestep Murong Ke until their zeal faded.

sentences.zh: 」閔怒曰：「吾成師以出，將平幽州，斬慕容雋。

translations.literal: " Ran Min angrily said, "I brought a finished army forth intending to pacify Youzhou and behead Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: " Ran Min retorted that he had marched to flatten Youzhou and take Murong Jun's head.

sentences.zh: 今遇恪而避之，人將侮我矣。

translations.literal: Now if I meet Ke and avoid him, people will mock me.
translations.idiomatic: Backing away from Murong Ke would make him a laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 」乃與恪遇，十戰皆敗之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he engaged Ke and defeated him in ten encounters.
translations.idiomatic: " He closed with Murong Ke and won ten straight skirmishes.

sentences.zh: 恪乃以鐵鎖連馬，簡善射鮮卑勇而無剛者五千，方陣而前。

translations.literal: Ke then chained horses with iron links, picked five thousand Xianbei who shot well yet lacked stubborn nerve, and advanced in square formation.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke locked mounts with iron chains and sent five thousand flexible Xianbei bowmen forward in a tight square.

sentences.zh: 閔所乘赤馬曰硃龍，日行千里，左杖雙刃矛，右執鉤戟，順風擊之，斬鮮卑三百餘級。

translations.literal: Ran Min's red horse was called Zhu Long; it covered a thousand li a day; he bore a double-edged spear in his left hand and a hooked halberd in his right; riding the wind he struck and beheaded more than three hundred Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: His charger Zhu Long—said to run a thousand li a day—carried him as he wielded twin-headed spear and hook halberd and cut down three hundred Xianbei in the gust.

sentences.zh: 俄而燕騎大至，圍之數周。

translations.literal: Soon Yan cavalry arrived in strength and ringed him round after round.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yan horse flooded in and wound coil after coil around him.

sentences.zh: 閔眾寡不敵，躍馬潰圍東走，行二十餘里，馬無故而死，為恪所擒，及董閏、張溫等送之於薊。

translations.literal: Ran Min was outnumbered; he vaulted his horse through the cordon and fled east; after twenty-some li the horse died for no clear reason; Ke captured him together with Dong Run, Zhang Wen and others and sent them to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Outmatched, he punched through eastward until his mount dropped dead twenty li out; Murong Ke seized him along with Dong Run and Zhang Wen and shipped them to Ji.

sentences.zh: 俊立閔而問之曰：「汝奴僕下才，何自妄稱天子？

translations.literal: Jun made Ran Min stand and asked him, "You are mean talent of slave stock—how dare you style yourself Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun had Ran Min stand trial: "A menial upstart—what right had you to call yourself emperor?

sentences.zh: 」閔曰：「天下大亂，爾曹夷狄，人面獸心，尚欲篡逆。

translations.literal: " Ran Min said, "All under heaven is in great chaos; you people are barbarian Di—human faces with beasts' hearts—and still you scheme usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: " Ran Min shot back that barbarians with human masks still plotted treason while the realm burned.

sentences.zh: 我一時英雄，何為不可作帝王邪！

translations.literal: I am a hero of the age—why may I not be emperor!
translations.idiomatic: He insisted a man of his stature could wear the purple.

sentences.zh: 」俊怒，鞭之三百，送于龍城，告廆、皝廟。

translations.literal: " Jun was angry, flogged him three hundred strokes, sent him to Longcheng, and reported the matter at the shrines of Gui and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: " Murong Jun flogged him three hundred times, sent him to Longcheng, and notified the shrines of Murong Gui and Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 遣慕容評率眾圍鄴。

translations.literal: He dispatched Murong Ping leading a host to besiege Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Murong Ping to invest Ye.

sentences.zh: 劉甯及弟崇帥胡騎三千奔于晉陽，蘇亥棄常山奔於新興。

translations.literal: Liu Ning and his younger brother Chong led three thousand Hu cavalry to Jinyang; Su Hai abandoned Changshan for Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ning and Liu Chong galloped three thousand Hu riders to Jinyang while Su Hai fled Changshan for Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 鄴中饑，人相食，季龍時宮人被食略盡。

translations.literal: Ye starved; people ate one another; palace women from Shi Hu's time were nearly all consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Ye cannibalism reigned and Shi Hu's former palace women were eaten to the last.

sentences.zh: 冉智尚幼，蔣幹遣侍中繆嵩、詹事劉猗奉表歸順，且乞師于晉。

translations.literal: Ran Zhi was still young; Jiang Gan sent attendant-in-chamber Miao Song and household mentor Liu Yi with a memorial of submission and a plea for Jin reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Ran Zhi was a child; Jiang Gan sent Miao Song and Liu Yi to declare allegiance and beg Eastern Jin for troops.

sentences.zh: 濮陽太守戴施自倉垣次於棘津，止猗，不聽進，責其傳國璽。

translations.literal: Puyang governor Dai Shi moved from Cangyuan to Jijin, stopped Liu Yi from advancing, and demanded the imperial seal.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shi blocked Liu Yi at Jijin and insisted on the Heirloom Seal.

sentences.zh: 猗使嵩還鄴復命，幹沈吟未決，施乃率壯士百餘人入鄴，助守三臺，譎之曰：「且出璽付我。

translations.literal: Yi sent Song back to Ye to report; Gan hesitated; Shi then led more than a hundred stalwarts into Ye, helped guard the Three Terraces, and deceived him, saying, "For now bring the seal out to me.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi sent Miao Song home while Jiang Gan wavered; Dai Shi slipped into Ye with a hundred braves, reinforced the Three Terraces, and coaxed Jiang Gan to hand over the seal.

sentences.zh: 今凶寇在外，道路不通，未敢送也。

translations.literal: Now fierce bandits are outside; roads are blocked—I dare not send it yet.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed bandits cut the roads and the seal could not travel.

sentences.zh: 須得璽，當馳白天子耳。

translations.literal: Once I hold the seal I can gallop to report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Possession would let him notify the emperor at speed.

sentences.zh: 天子聞璽已在吾處，信卿至誠，必遣軍糧厚相救餉。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven learns the seal is with me he will trust your utmost sincerity and surely dispatch grain and troops in generous relief.
translations.idiomatic: The court would trust their loyalty and flood Ye with supplies once the seal rested with Dai Shi.

sentences.zh: 」幹以為然，乃出璽付之。

translations.literal: " Gan thought it right and brought out the seal and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang Gan agreed and surrendered the Heirloom Seal.

sentences.zh: 施宣言使督護何融迎糧，陰令懷璽送于京師。

translations.literal: Shi publicly declared he was sending protector-general He Rong to welcome grain while secretly ordering him to carry the seal to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shi announced grain convoys under He Rong but secretly smuggled the seal toward Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 長水校尉馬願、龍驤田香開門降評。

translations.literal: Colonel of changshui Ma Yuan and dragon soaring Tian Xiang opened the gates and surrendered to Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan and Tian Xiang threw open Ye's gates to Murong Ping.

sentences.zh: 施、融、蔣幹懸縋而下，奔於倉垣。

translations.literal: Shi, Rong, and Jiang Gan were lowered by ropes and fled to Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shi, He Rong, and Jiang Gan rappelled the walls and escaped to Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 評送閔妻董氏、太子智、太尉申鐘、司空條攸、中書監聶熊，司隸校尉籍羆、中書令李垣及諸王公卿士于薊。

translations.literal: Ping sent Ran Min's wife Lady Dong, heir Zhi, grand commandant Shen Zhong, minister of works Tiao You, palace secretariat overseer Nie Xiong, metropolitan commandant Ji Pi, palace secretariat director Li Yuan, and various royal dukes and ministers to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping shipped Lady Dong, Ran Zhi, Grand Commandant Shen Zhong, minister Tiao You, Nie Xiong, Ji Pi, Li Yuan, and the captured ministers to Ji.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王簡、左僕射張乾、右僕射郎肅自殺。

translations.literal: Masters-of-Book chief Wang Jian, left vice-director Zhang Qian, and right vice-director Lang Su killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Zhang Qian, and Lang Su committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 俊送閔既至龍城，斬於遏陘山。

translations.literal: After Jun sent Ran Min and he reached Longcheng, he executed him at Ejing Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun had Ran Min executed at Ejing Mountain once he reached Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 山左右七里草木悉枯，蝗蟲大起，五月不雨，至於十二月。

translations.literal: For seven li around the mountain grass and trees withered; locusts swarmed; from the fifth month until the twelfth no rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Vegetation withered for seven li around, locusts boiled up, and drought gripped from May through December.

sentences.zh: 俊遣使者祀之，諡曰武悼天王，其日大雪。

translations.literal: Jun dispatched envoys to sacrifice to him, gave him the posthumous title Martial-Lament Heavenly King, and that day great snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun offered sacrifice, canonized him Martial-Lament Heavenly King, and snow fell that same day.

sentences.zh: 是歲永和八年也。

translations.literal: That year was the eighth year of Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: The year was Yonghe 8.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historical appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Section rubric: historians' verdict.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫拯溺救焚，帝王之師也；

translations.literal: The historians say: Dragging the drowning from the flood and rescue from fire belong to the armies of true kings;
translations.idiomatic: The chroniclers declare that pulling victims from flood and flame marks legitimate imperial hosts;

sentences.zh: 窮凶騁暴，戎狄之舉也。

translations.literal: Running riot in utmost cruelty is the way of Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: unbridled cruelty is the barbarians' habit.

sentences.zh: 蠢茲雜種，自古為虞，限以塞垣，猶懼侵軼，況乃入居中壤，窺我王政，乘弛紊之機，睹危亡之隙，而莫不嘯群鳴鏑，汨亂天常者乎！

translations.literal: These foolish mixed breeds have been a scourge since antiquity; penned behind frontier walls we still feared their raids—how much worse when they occupy the central lands, spy on our royal rule, seize slack and disorder, spy gaps of peril and ruin, and every one howls with clans and whistles arrows to overturn heaven's constant!
translations.idiomatic: Such mongrel peoples troubled China for ages; even behind the long walls their raids terrified—yet once they seized the heartland, watched our throne stumble, and exploited every crack, none failed to rally kin, loose shafts, and smash natural order.

sentences.zh: 石勒出自羌渠，見奇丑類。

translations.literal: Shi Le sprang from the Qiangqu branch and stood out odd among base stock.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le rose from Qiangqu herdsmen and seemed freakish among riffraff.

sentences.zh: 聞鞞上党，季子鑒其非凡；

translations.literal: When drums sounded in Shangdang, Jizi judged him no ordinary man;
translations.idiomatic: His drums in Shangdang told Ji Zi he was no common soldier;

sentences.zh: 倚嘯洛城，夷甫識其為亂。

translations.literal: when he whistled leaning on Luoyang's walls, Yifu knew him for trouble.
translations.idiomatic: his whistle against Luoyang warned Wang Yan he would bring ruin.

sentences.zh: 及惠皇失統，宇內崩離，遂乃招聚蟻徒，乘間煽禍，虔劉我都邑，翦害我黎元。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui lost the reins and the realm shattered, he gathered ant-like followers, fanned disaster through every opening, slaughtered our capitals, and mowed down our people.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Hui lost control and the empire flew apart, he rallied mobs, fed on every breach, butchered our cities, and cut down the common folk.

sentences.zh: 朝市淪胥，若沈航於鯨浪；

translations.literal: Court and market sank together like boats swallowed in the jaws of whale waves;
translations.idiomatic: Capital life vanished as if ships pulled under by leviathan seas;

sentences.zh: 王公顛仆，譬游魂于龍漠。

translations.literal: princes of blood fell headlong like wandering souls adrift on dragon-haunted deserts.
translations.idiomatic: royal princes toppled like souls lost on sands stalked by dragons.

sentences.zh: 豈天厭晉德而假茲妖孽者歟！

translations.literal: Could it be that Heaven had tired of Jin virtue and lent these monsters their hour!
translations.idiomatic: Had Heaven wearied of Jin and leased its mandate to fiends?

sentences.zh: 觀其對敵臨危，運籌賈勇，奇謨間發，猛氣橫飛。

translations.literal: Observe him facing foes and peril—laying plans, summoning valor—strange stratagems flashing forth, fierce breath sweeping wide.
translations.idiomatic: Yet facing blades he spun plots and summoned courage—clever strikes, sudden bursts of terrible daring.

sentences.zh: 遠嗤魏武，則風情慷慨；

translations.literal: From afar he mocked Wei Wu—his mood lofty and bold;
translations.idiomatic: He sneered at Cao Cao from the distance, voice ringing with boast;

sentences.zh: 近答劉琨，則音詞倜儻。

translations.literal: replying to Liu Kun near at hand, his words rang free and gallant.
translations.idiomatic: yet answering Liu Kun his tone stayed fluent and bold.

sentences.zh: 焚元超於苦縣，陳其亂政之愆；

translations.literal: At Ku county he burned Sima Yue—courtesy Yuan Chao—displaying the indictment of his ruinous rule;
translations.idiomatic: At Ku he cremated Sima Yue and aired the indictment of his misgovernment;

sentences.zh: 戮彭祖于襄國，數以無君之罪。

translations.literal: at Xiangguo he executed Wang Yan, detailing his crimes of fealty abandoned toward his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: at Xiangguo he cut down Wang Yan and rehearsed how he betrayed his king.

sentences.zh: 於是跨躡燕、趙，併吞韓、魏，杖奇材而竊徽號，擁舊都而抗王室，褫毯裘，襲冠帶，釋介胄，開庠序，鄰敵懼威而獻款，絕域承風而納貢，則古之為國，曷以加諸！

translations.literal: Thereupon he strode Yan and Zhao, swallowed Han and Wei, leaned on prodigious talent to steal august titles, hugged the old capital and defied the royal house—casting off felt and fur, donning cap and sash, laying aside mail and helm, opening schools—while neighboring foes offered tribute from fear and distant lands carried gifts on the wind—what ancient state surpassed such sway!
translations.idiomatic: Thus he overran the north, crowned himself, occupied Luoyang yet challenged Jin—barbarian turned mandarin, warrior turned patron of learning—until neighbors bought peace with tribute and distant shores sent gifts—few empires of old outshone that brief zenith.

sentences.zh: 雖曰凶殘，亦一時傑也。

translations.literal: Though called cruel, he was nonetheless a champion of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Savage he was—yet peerless in his moment.

sentences.zh: 而托授非所，貽厥無謀，身隕嗣滅，業歸攜養，斯乃知人之暗焉。

translations.literal: Yet his chosen heirs were wrong; he left no worthy plan—himself destroyed, sons extinguished, enterprise handed to an adopted shoot—such was his blindness in judging men.
translations.idiomatic: Wrong heirs and no legacy—death of line, throne lost to adopted Jinu—proof he could not read men.

sentences.zh: 季龍心昧德義，幼而輕險，假豹姿於羊質，騁梟心於狼性，始懷怨懟，終行篡奪。

translations.literal: Jilong's heart was blind to virtue and duty—already in youth reckless and vicious—borrowing a leopard's coat on a sheep's frame, unleashing an owl's heart within a wolf nature—first nursing resentment, finally usurping.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu cloaked wolf cruelty in borrowed grandeur—from spiteful youth to regicide.

sentences.zh: 於是窮驕極侈，勞役繁興，畚鍤相尋，干戈不息，刑政嚴酷，動見誅夷，惵惵遺黎，求哀無地，戎狄殘獷，斯為甚乎！

translations.literal: Thereupon pride and extravagance reached extremes—corvée multiplied without cease, shovel and spear pursued one another without pause—punishments harsh beyond measure, executions everywhere—common survivors trembled with nowhere to plead—among barbarian cruelty none exceeded this!
translations.idiomatic: Corvée, war, and torture consumed the realm—no plea left for the trembling millions—few barbarities matched his.

sentences.zh: 既而父子猜嫌，兄弟仇隙，自相屠膾，取笑天下。

translations.literal: Soon father and son eyed each other with suspicion; brothers nursed mutual hatred—slaughtering kin themselves until All-under-Heaven laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Kin turned butcher—father feuding sons, brothers at throats—mockery across the world.

sentences.zh: 墳土未燥，禍亂薦臻，釁起于張豺，族傾于冉閔，積惡致滅，有天道哉！

translations.literal: Earth on the tomb still damp, calamity piled anew—strife rose with Zhang Chao, lineage toppled under Ran Min—accumulated evil brought extinction: does Heaven not reckon accounts!
translations.idiomatic: Fresh graves, fresh wars—Zhang Chao lit the fuse, Ran Min erased the clan—payback written in heaven's ledger.

sentences.zh: 夫從逆則凶，事符影響；

translations.literal: To follow rebellion is to invite calamity—the tally matches shadow to echo;
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion buys ruin—cause and echo align;

sentences.zh: 為咎必應，理若迴圈。

translations.literal: disaster answering guilt moves like a turning wheel.
translations.idiomatic: guilt wheels back as doom.

sentences.zh: 世龍之殪晉人，既窮其酷；

translations.literal: Shilong's slaughter of Jin people already exhausted cruelty;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le's massacre of Han Chinese plumbed cruelty's depths;

sentences.zh: 永曾之誅羯士，亦殲其類。

translations.literal: Yongzeng's extermination of Jie warriors likewise wiped their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Yongzeng's purge of the Jie matched it in kind.

sentences.zh: 無德不報，斯之謂乎！

translations.literal: Virtue unrewarded goes unpaid—does not this saying fit!
translations.idiomatic: What goes around returns—was it not so here?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：中朝不競，蠻狄爭衡。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The central court lost its edge; barbarians contested the scales.
translations.idiomatic: Verse: Central Jin faltered while northern tribes wrestled for supremacy;

sentences.zh: 塵飛五嶽，霧晻三精。

translations.literal: Dust flew across the Five March ranges; mist swallowed the Three Essences.
translations.idiomatic: dust veiled the sacred peaks and stars hid their light;

sentences.zh: 狡焉石氏，怙亂窮兵。

translations.literal: Crafty stood House Shi, clinging to chaos and exhausting armies.
translations.idiomatic: the Shi clan thrived on turmoil and endless war;

sentences.zh: 流災肆慝，剽邑屠城。

translations.literal: Calamity flowed and malice spread—storming towns, slaughtering cities.
translations.idiomatic: disaster followed malice—cities sacked, streets red;

sentences.zh: 始自群盜，終假鴻名。

translations.literal: Beginning as mere bandits, they ended clutching a mighty name.
translations.idiomatic: from hill-bandits they stole an emperor's title;

sentences.zh: 勿謂凶醜，亦曰時英。

translations.literal: Do not call them merely ogres—they too were heroes of the hour.
translations.idiomatic: call them brutes, yet they were titans of their age;

sentences.zh: 季龍篡奪，淫虐播聲。

translations.literal: Jilong usurped the throne and broadcast lustful cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu seized the throne and spread debauched terror;

sentences.zh: 身喪國泯，其由禍盈。

translations.literal: His body lost, state extinguished—such was the reckoning when guilt overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: when malice brimmed over, man perished and kingdom vanished.
